articles.title: Git security vulnerabilities announced
articles.summary:
Today, the Git project is releasing new versions to address six security vulnerabilities. These include arbitrary code execution when recursively cloning a malicious repository, writes to unintended files, and memory corruption when processing merges or binary patches.
The fixes are included in Git 2.56.1, with backports to Git 2.55.1, 2.54.1, 2.53.1, 2.52.1, 2.51.3, and 2.50.2. We recommend updating to Git 2.56.1 or the patched release for your maintenance series, and updating any applications that bundle Git.
Vulnerabilities in Git
CVE-2026-111760: Code execution during recursive clones
Git checks paths before writing files into a working tree, including rejecting paths that would overwrite its own repository metadata. However, an integer truncation in Git’s index handling can cause an extremely long path to pass validation under one name and then be written using a shorter name.
An attacker can use this discrepancy to replace a submodule’s .git file with a symbolic link pointing to a directory containing malicious configuration or hooks. When Git subsequently uses that directory, it can execute attacker-controlled code during a recursive clone.
The fix rejects extremely long index entry paths before their lengths can be truncated.
[Advisory]
CVE-2026-113408: Path traversal through a server’s advertised HEAD

articles.title: Anthropic Rolls Out Mythos 5.2 With Improved Bug Hunting, Fewer Sandbox Escapes
articles.summary:
Anthropic on Monday released Claude Mythos 5.2, the latest version of its access-restricted AI model, and Mozilla says it roughly doubled the vulnerability discovery results of Mythos 5.1 in Firefox.
Mythos 5.2 and Claude Fable 5.2, which was released alongside it, share the same underlying model. The difference lies in the guardrails: Fable, which anyone can use, carries protections against cybersecurity and biology misuse, while Mythos ships without some of them.
Direct access to Mythos is reserved for vetted organizations, which can apply through Anthropic’s Cyber and Life Sciences Verification Programs.
“We’ve worked closely with the Anthropic team all year to harden Firefox with successive generations of Claude models, and each round has left fewer, subtler bugs to find. Even so, Mythos 5.2 roughly doubled the vulnerability discovery metrics of Mythos 5.1 across respective scanning campaigns,” said Brian Grinstead, distinguished engineer at Mozilla.
Internally, Anthropic measures progress with CVE Rediscovery, which gives a model the code of a project from before a known CVE was patched and checks whether the model spots the flaw without help.
In an October run covering 1,829 CVEs, Mythos 5.2 achieved a success rate of 89.6%. Mythos 5.1 scored 78.3%, and Opus 5.5, tested without safeguards, scored 81.3%.

articles.title: Speech Processing Pioneer Bishnu Saroop Atal Dies at 93
articles.summary:
Bishnu Saroop Atal
Acoustics and signal processing pioneer
Life Fellow, 93; died 19 August
Atal was an acoustics and signal processing researcher at Bell Labs in Murray Hill, N.J., and later at AT&T’s Shannon Laboratory, in Florham Park, N.J. His pioneering work on voice-coding techniques became the foundation for efficient, high-quality voice transmission over cellular networks. He received the 2013 IEEE Jack S. Kilby Signal Processing Medal for “fundamental and pioneering contributions to speech coding.”
He joined Bell Labs in 1961 as a communications researcher, and his early work there focused on speaker identification technology. During the 1960s he helped develop linear predictive coding, a powerful method for analyzing and compressing speech. LPC is now the most widely used method for encoding speech at a low bit rate.
Atal developed increasingly sophisticated low-bit-rate speech-coding techniques. They included multipulse LPC, which improved the quality of compressed speech.
Bishnu Saroop AtalNokia Bell Labs
He also worked with his colleague Manfred R. Schroeder to develop code-excited linear prediction, a method for producing high-quality speech at very low bit rates. CELP became a foundational technique in modern speech coding, letting digital communications systems carry voice using less bandwidth. The extra efficiency expanded cellular capacity, allowing wireless networks to handle more simultaneous calls.

The AI Security Gap Hiding in Routine Maintenance
Abby Kearns | 10 November 2026
This blog was first published on November 9, 2026 at https://openssf.org/blog/2026/11/09/the-ai-security-gap-hiding-in-routine-maintenance/ and repurposed here with consent from the author.
Ask a security team what worries them about AI and you'll probably hear about supply chain attacks or prompt injection first. The Linux Foundation's new report, State of AI Impact on Software Security and Cybersecurity 2026, backs that up, with 93% of the security experts it surveyed concerned about supply chain attacks and 90% about prompt injection. Some of the report's most important findings, though, are about something a lot less dramatic: the everyday work of keeping software up to date.
LF Research surveyed 308 people working on security in companies and open source projects this summer, in research sponsored by OpenSSF, LF AI & Data, and ActiveState, where I'm CEO. Coming at it as an operator, I wasn't surprised by what they found, because every dependency a team adds comes with years of upkeep, and that work almost never gets staffed the way new features do.
Where teams feel least prepared
The survey asked practitioners how concerned they are about a long list of AI-related threats and how prepared they feel for each one, and for every single threat, concern came out ahead. NVIDIA is also contributing to Agent Substrate, an open source Google-led framework for operating long-running agent workloads at scale on Kubernetes that has been accepted into the CNCF Sandbox.

articles.title: Black Friday: Warum die Rabattschlacht schon jetzt tobt
articles.summary:
Frühe Black-Friday-Angebote: Lohnt sich der Kauf schon jetzt?
Wir schauen auf den Kalender und reiben uns verwundert die Augen: Der Black Friday ist erst am 27. November – und doch wirbt gefühlt schon die halbe Branche mit dem Schnäppchen-Schlagwort, das die preisbewussten Kund:innen in Wallung bringen soll. Und die Geschäfte sind erfinderisch: Pre-Black-Friday-Angebote, Early-Black-Friday-Deals und Black Weeks sind nur ein paar der kreativen Wortschöpfungen, die allesamt nur eins suggerieren sollen: Billiger wird’s so schnell nicht mehr.
Man könnte fast glauben, der Handel hätte Angst, den Black Friday zu verpassen. Doch in Wahrheit laufen vor allem die Händler dem Geld ihrer Kund hinterher. Dass sie damit seit Jahren immer früher anfangen, hat einen Grund, der insbesondere in diesem Jahr eine große Rolle spielen könnte: Die Kund:innen können ihr Weihnachtsgeld, so sie es überhaupt noch bekommen, schließlich nur einmal ausgeben.
Und wer hier früher dran ist als die anderen, so das Kalkül, hat größere Chancen darauf. Wer also sein Budget bereits Anfang November bei Händler A gelassen hat, fällt Ende November womöglich als Kunde für Händler B aus.
Die Angst, zu früh gekauft zu haben
Doch gerade in wirtschaftlich angespannten Zeiten überlegen Verbraucher:innen genauer, wofür sie ihr Erspartes ausgeben. Schon länger beobachten Marktforscher:innen gar nicht mal so sehr eine Kaufzurückhaltung, wohl aber, dass die Verbraucher:innen bis zum November mit wichtigen Anschaffungen warte…

articles.title: Over a Dozen Organizations Hit in Qubole Supply Chain Attack
articles.summary:
A threat actor used the compromised IAM credentials for an AWS account associated with big-data platform Qubole to steal data from over a dozen organizations, cybersecurity researchers discovered.
The credentials allowed the attackers to assume IAM roles organizations had set up for Qubole’s AWS account and access their AWS environments.
Cross-account IAM roles are normal for SaaS platforms that operate within customers’ AWS environments. During onboarding, customers create a role for Qubole, and the vendor’s AWS account can assume the role when needed, typically via an External ID.
The leaked Qubole credentials allowed the threat actor to assume this role and pull data from the AWS environments of over a dozen companies.
“The doors the attacker used were old ones. Qubole roles were still in place long after companies had stopped using Qubole, and those roles could read nearly all of the data the attacker went after,” cybersecurity firm Sentra notes.
The roles stayed dormant until the campaign kicked off on October 14. They were used until October 26 to enumerate resources, collect secrets and configurations, and access data.
The attacks came from a rented OVH server and the Mullvad VPN, and none of the observed activity originated from Qubole’s network, Sentra says.

articles.title: Fireworks AI discloses new breach after cloud provider hack
articles.summary:
AI infrastructure startup Fireworks has disclosed a new security breach in which attackers accessed its development machines after breaching a third-party cloud provider.
FireWorks provides a high-performance inference platform for developers who want to deploy and run open-source artificial intelligence models (such as Mistral, Meta's Llama, or Google's Gemma) without worrying about hardware bottlenecks and complex infrastructure tasks.
The company notified law enforcement and customers of another security incident in early October after attackers accessed environment variables containing API keys and tokens stored as secrets for a limited number of accounts.
"The evidence indicates links to a cybercriminal threat actor group, which is financially motivated and aimed at selling tokens from unauthorized access to Large Language Models (LLMs) to illicit routing gateways, known as 'LLMJacking'," Fireworks said at the time.
After revoking compromised internal credentials, affected Fireworks API keys, and keys created by the attackers, Fireworks discovered another security incident on October 23.
In the new breach, the threat actors accessed resource metadata (e.g., Fireworks resource identifiers, display names, descriptions, creation time), billing information (e.g., billing and shipping addresses, invoice and payment history, account balance, and credit usage), and incomplete model weights and datasets for some customers.

articles.title: VC exits show year-over-year improvement as acquisitions ramp up: CVCA report
articles.summary:
The disclosed value of VC exits in Canada has more than doubled so far compared to last year as the ecosystem eagerly anticipates an influx of capital in the coming years.
The total amount invested hit $4.3 billion CAD across 397 deals through the first three quarters of 2026.
According to the Canadian Venture Capital & Private Equity Association’s Q3 2026 report on Canadian venture deals, mergers and acquisitions accounted for 26 out of the 28 venture-backed exits during the year’s first three quarters. There were only 29 exits in total last year. Proceeds totalled $744 million CAD across 10 disclosed transactions, which is more than double the $355 million in disclosed exit value for all of 2025.
But while 2026 venture-backed merger and acquisition (M&A) activity has already surpassed 2025 numbers, last year was far below 2023 and 2024, which both recorded more than 30 exits.
Some of the largest acquisitions included an $850-million CAD go-private deal for Calgary’s Blackline Safety and the reported $400-million USD purchase of Montréal amateur sports streamer LiveBarn. Meanwhile, one of 2026’s largest exits—the semiconductor company Taalas, which chip giant AMD has agreed to buy for $2.9 billion USD—has yet to close, meaning that it’s not included in CVCA’s exit total. The $4.75-billion USD deal to acquire CoolIT Systems, which passed from KKR to Ecolab, was classified as a private equity transaction, and was also therefore not added to the total.

WhatsApp has grown into one of the most popular messaging apps in the world, used by over 3 billion people. But with that growth, the app has also become complex, packing in features like communities, channels, stories and business features, and a lot of people find it hard to navigate.
Kunal Shah, who took over leadership of the app’s development from Will Cathcart earlier this year, now wants to make the app and actions within it simpler to use. In a new note shared on Tuesday, Shah said the company wants to make voice notes, groups, stickers, and video “simpler and more expressive.”
WhatsApp has long also tried to develop an ecosystem that lets users explore products and make purchases, and Shah’s note indicates more of that is coming, hinting at partnerships with payment companies and telecom providers to enable bill payment, loans, and eSIM purchases.
Shah also said the company wants to use AI to surface important information to users.
“It should quickly find what you need, get things done, and make sure you never miss a booking or an appointment. The best technology saves you time, so you can get back to the connections that matter,” he wrote.
WhatsApp currently offers an AI assistant that can summarize messages and create drafts. It’s not clear if the company will use its Muse agent to collate information and send reminders to people.

articles.title: Microsoft Fixes Nearly 1,100 Security Vulnerabilities
articles.summary:
Microsoft did another four-digit patch drop today, releasing updates to fix almost 1,100 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and supported software. This month’s Patch Tuesday addresses 63 critical flaws — including a zero-day in Microsoft Outlook — and comes amid important security updates from other software makers, including Adobe, Apple, Google and Mozilla.
November’s patch release from Redmond tackles 1,093 vulnerabilities, fixing 63 “critical” flaws that can be exploited to seize control over a Windows system with little or no help from users. Nearly half of those critical bugs are remote code execution vulnerabilities. Overall, 535 of the flaws addressed this month allow an attacker to elevate their privileges on a vulnerable device.
This latest round of updates means Microsoft has shipped more than 5,100 security patches so far this year, a staggering number considering that a year ago Microsoft was averaging around 100 patches per month. Microsoft credits advances in artificial intelligence for helping to find (and fix) such a large volume of security bugs in recent months. Last month, Microsoft pushed more than 1,400 fixes.
According to Redmond, just one of the flaws is already seeing active exploitation: CVE-2026-124194, a spoofing bug in Outlook. The advisory for CVE-2026-124194 says it affects Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise and editions of Microsoft Office.

articles.title: SAP Patches Critical ICM2SHELL, ProxyGate Vulnerabilities
articles.summary:
Enterprise software maker SAP on Tuesday announced the release of 42 new and updated security notes, including nine that resolve critical-severity vulnerabilities.
Four of SAP’s new security notes address maximum-severity flaws in NetWeaver (Internet Communication Manager (ICM) and SAML2 Service Provider), Web Dispatcher, and Gateway.
The ICM and Web Dispatcher flaws, tracked as CVE-2026-76964 and CVE-2026-89126, are a single weakness in the SAP kernel component that receives HTTP, HTTPS, and WebSocket traffic.
According to Onapsis, which calls the security defect ICM2SHELL, the issue is related to reassembling large WebSocket messages, which may be split into fragments during a server-browser exchange and then put together by the receiver.
“A specially crafted sequence of WebSocket messages makes the ICM or the WD write attacker-controlled data past the end of the memory it reserved for the connection. Depending on how that data is shaped, the result is either an immediate crash of the process or controlled corruption of its memory,” Onapsis explains.
ICM2SHELL, the enterprise application security firm says, could allow an attacker to execute operating system commands with <sid>adm privileges.

articles.title: How AI Helps Recyclers Turn Mixed Waste Into Reusable Material
articles.summary:
As world leaders gather for COP31 in Türkiye, the event’s emphasis on zero waste puts a practical challenge in focus: how to keep products and materials in use for longer. Globally, less than 7% of the materials entering the economy come from recycled or reused sources. Municipal solid waste generation accounts for over 2 billion tons of trash per year — a figure that could nearly double by 2050.
AI and robotics are helping change this trajectory, as innovators around the globe improve sorting to recover resources that would otherwise end up in landfills.
“A more circular economy relies on making better use of what we already have,” said Josh Parker, head of sustainability at NVIDIA. “AI can help us understand what’s in a waste stream, identify what can be recovered and automate the work of sorting it. We’re giving innovators the computing tools to make those processes more effective and bring them to more places.”
See how four members of the NVIDIA Inception program for startups are applying AI to keep valuable materials in circulation.
Recycled plastic is only used if its cost and quality can compete with new material. Too often it can’t: Incoming waste is of inconsistent quality, sorting depends on hard-to-find manual labor and mixed scrap ends up downcycled into low-grade products.

Bereits vor der offiziellen Vorstellung berichtet Euronews über die wichtigsten Eckpunkte des Vorschlags. Demnach listet der Vorschlag detailliert sogenannte „Dark Patterns“ auf, also manipulative Designelemente, die Nutzer:innen oft unbemerkt zu bestimmten Entscheidungen motivieren.
Dazu gehört etwa ein Webdesign, das es leicht macht, einen Vertrag abzuschließen, den Weg zur Kündigung aber erschwert. Ebenso zählt dazu, Preise und Bedingungen zur automatischen Vertragsverlängerung absichtlich so zu platzieren, dass sie nur schwer zu finden sind.

NVIDIA is announcing two open source projects for building and operating managed Kubernetes services on GPU infrastructure—NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine (NVKE) and NVIDIA Kubernetes Recipes (NVKR). Both are new projects available in public preview.
AI Factory customers often want to consume GPU capacity through the Kubernetes APIs, tools, and ecosystem they already use, with the factory operating their clusters. Delivering this service requires API-driven provisioning, tenant isolation, upgrades, and recovery, backed by service commitments. It also requires qualifying GPU hardware, networking, drivers, and runtime software across GPU generations and Kubernetes versions.
NVKE and NVKR divide this work between cluster management and reproducible software builds. NVKE provides the software to run a managed Kubernetes service, installed on the factory’s infrastructure, with APIs to provision and manage clusters. NVKR builds the operating system images, container images, and packages those clusters need, using recipes that define validated combinations of software versions and GPU generations. AI Factories retain control of their software, operations, service, and customer experience. Teams can adopt NVKE and NVKR projects together or independently.

articles.title: Mazda promet 703 km d’autonomie sur sa nouvelle 6e, mais lisez bien les petites lignes
articles.summary:

Lors de mon essai publié en février, j’avais relevé un amortissement manquant de cohérence (tantôt souple, tantôt sec), une autonomie juste pour une berline routière, une recharge trop lente sur la version Grande Autonomie, des aides à la conduite à revoir et un système multimédia à la ramasse.
Le millésime 2027, que Mazda a présenté ce lundi 9 novembre, corrige une partie de ces défauts avec sa nouvelle (et unique) batterie, sa suspension recalibrée et ses ADAS revues. Le tout pour un prix toujours aussi intéressant : à partir de 43 900 €.
703 km d’autonomie, mais en ville
Pour mémoire, la 6e imposait jusqu’ici un choix absurde. La version de base, avec sa batterie LFP de 68,8 kWh acceptait 165 kW en recharge rapide mais plafonnait à 479 km WLTP. Quant à la Grande Autonomie de 80 kWh, elle allait jusqu’à 552 km, mais était bridée à 90 kW et demandait 47 minutes pour passer de 10 à 80 %, soit deux fois plus que la petite batterie.
Le millésime 2027 remplace les deux accumulateurs par une seule batterie LFP de 78 kWh, qui accepte jusqu’à 200 kW. Elle est alimentée par le même moteur de 258 ch (placé à l’arrière) de l’ancienne version à petite batterie.
Attention à la lecture de la fiche technique. Le communiqué français met en avant « jusqu’à 703 km d’autonomie en cycle urbain ». La « vraie » autonomie théorique en cycle mixte de la 6e est 560 km WLTP, comme le confirme Mazda dans son communiqué …

articles.title: Google patches eighth Chrome zero-day exploited in attacks this year
articles.summary:
Google has released emergency security updates to patch a new Chrome vulnerability exploited in zero-day attacks, the eighth such flaw since the start of the year.
"Google is aware that an exploit for CVE-2026-125350 exists in the wild," the company said in a Monday security advisory.
As Google explained, this flaw stems from a Use-After-Free (UAF) weakness in the XML component of the Google Chrome web browser, which occurs when the browser's XML parser processes data, deletes an object from the computer's memory, but fails to clear the pointer referencing that object.
Attackers can exploit this high-severity memory corruption vulnerability when the browser later tries to use or read that "freed" memory space to manipulate the memory layout and execute malicious code.
While Google has found evidence of attackers exploiting this zero-day bug in the wild, it has not shared additional details about these incidents.
"Access to bug details and links may be kept restricted until a majority of users are updated with a fix. We will also retain restrictions if the bug exists in a third party library that other projects similarly depend on, but haven't yet fixed," it noted.
Google has now fixed the zero-day for users in the Stable Desktop channel, with new versions rolling out to Windows, macOS (157.0.8103.50/.51), and Linux users (157.0.8103.50). articles.title: Lazare, veni foras: Reprogramming Dormant Neurons to Backdoor AI Agents - Microsoft Research
articles.summary:
Microsoft researchers have discovered “Lazarus,” a backdoor technique that can reprogram dormant neurons in an AI model, causing an otherwise normal AI agent to execute malicious commands when a hidden trigger appears.
The threat is especially serious for AI agents with tool or terminal access. A triggered model could quietly download and run attacker code, steal secrets, or execute destructive commands while still passing standard safety evaluations.
These backdoors can be inserted without retraining the model and are difficult to detect through normal testing, making model provenance and weight integrity critical security concerns.
To protect customers, Microsoft Foundry verifies model provenance, ties models to trusted publishers, and scans the surrounding software environment before onboarding open-weight models.
Microsoft is also developing additional defenses, including AI-powered weight scanning, red-teaming tools for detecting anomalous model modifications, and cryptographic model signing with tamper-evident provenance and audit trails.
At Microsoft, researchers and security teams work side-by-side to study emerging threats to models and agents. Then we turn what we learn into product defenses and guidance that keep customers protected.
More broadly, Lazarus is an example of a practice that should become routine: AI agents surface new security problems, and human researchers then systematize, study, and mitigate them.

How connected inspection, metrology and software can help manufacturers move SiPh and CPO toward high-volume production.
More bandwidth. Lower latency. Less power consumed and less heat generated.
These are three of the challenges facing manufacturers as AI pushes electrical interconnects toward their limits. Silicon photonics (SiPh) and co-packaged optics (CPO) offer a path forward by using light to transmit data rather than relying solely on electrical signals. But realizing those benefits at production scale introduces another challenge: maintaining precise process control across the optical structures, materials and integration processes that ultimately determine device performance and yield.
At the same time, traditional copper interconnects face increasing resistance, electromigration and power challenges as semiconductor architectures scale (Figure 1). articles.title: Start and Restore GPU Workloads in Seconds with NVIDIA Snapshot | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
NVIDIA Snapshot, a new open-source component of the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform, makes initialized GPU workloads reusable across inference replicas—speeding startup and recovery.
When inference demand spikes or a replica fails, available GPUs don’t translate immediately into serving capacity. Initializing an LLM workload—a process known as a cold start—can take minutes, delaying scaling and recovery.
Snapshot is a checkpoint and restore system for GPU workloads on Kubernetes. It captures a fully initialized workload—including CPU and GPU memory—and restores that state on compatible infrastructure, bringing inference capacity online in seconds instead of minutes. Figure 1 shows the startup sequence. Snapshot skips repeated workload initialization; infrastructure provisioning and container image loading remain outside the measured restore path.
This post explains how Snapshot checkpoints and restores GPU workloads, how platform teams can integrate it, and how restore times compare with cold starts across three inference engines.
Snapshot for AI factory operations
Originally developed for NVIDIA Dynamo inference workers, Snapshot provides checkpoint and restore capabilities that other inference engines, schedulers, controllers, and platforms can integrate.
Snapshot provides two operations for GPU Pods:
- Checkpoint: Once a workload is fully initialized, capture its CPU and GPU memory as a portable artifact.

Mais ces boîtiers intelligents n’ont pas que des adeptes. Leur déploiement suscite encore de nombreuses contestations, les principaux arguments avancés étant les craintes liées aux ondes électromagnétiques et à la protection des données personnelles.

articles.title: “Ser despedido de Apple fue lo mejor que podría haberme pasado”: Así se reinventó Steve Jobs
articles.summary:
En 2005, ante los estudiantes de la Universidad de Stanford, Steve Jobs repasó tres episodios de su vida que habían definido su recorrido personal y profesional. Uno de ellos fue su salida de Apple, la empresa que había creado junto con Steve Wozniak cuando tenía 20 años y de la que fue apartado una década después.
El fundador describió aquel momento como una derrota pública y dolorosa. Pero, con la distancia que daban los años, sostuvo que “ser despedido de Apple fue lo mejor que podría haberme pasado”.
La ruptura lo llevó a fundar NeXT, a involucrarse en Pixar y, más tarde, a regresar a la compañía con una mirada distinta sobre el trabajo, el fracaso y la posibilidad de empezar otra vez.
Cómo pudo ser echado de la empresa que había fundado
Jobs recordó que Apple nació en el garaje de la casa de sus padres. Junto a Wozniak, pasó de un proyecto de dos personas a una empresa con 4.000 empleados y una valuación de 2.000 millones de dólares en apenas diez años.
Poco antes de cumplir 30, la compañía había presentado el Macintosh, al que definió como su creación más importante hasta ese momento. El crecimiento de Apple llevó a Jobs y a la dirección a incorporar a un ejecutivo para conducir la empresa con él.
Según relató, las diferencias sobre el futuro de la compañía crecieron hasta derivar en un enfrentamiento. El Consejo respaldó al otro directivo y Jobs quedó fuera de la firma. “Había desaparecido aquello que había ocupado el centro de toda mi vida adulta. Fue devastador”, rec…

articles.title: Jordi Cruz, sobre la actitud de los trabajadores: “Hay un cambio generacional. Hemos pasado de ser espartanos y meterle catorce horas a hacer ocho y entenderlo de una forma distinta”
articles.summary:
Es la época de las 14 horas versus las 8. Jordi Cruz habla de ese cambio de mentalidad en el sector hostelero. “Hay un cambio generacional”, afirma el cocinero en el pódcast Se me Antoja. Así explica en esta conversación cómo ha cambiado la mentalidad y las dificultades que tiene él para adaptarse.
El chef empezó a trabajar en cocina profesional con 14 años. Es uno de los rostros de la restauración (conocido por su restaurante ABaC y sus estrellas Michelin). También es jurado de MasterChef.
En su opinión, en 5 años ha cambiado la mentalidad. Antes era bonito y sacrificado. “Hemos pasado de ser espartanos, de meterle 14 horas”, afirma. Ahora hay que buscar un equilibrio y “hacer solo ocho horas”.
Esto tiene que ver con el cambio de mentalidad respecto al oficio. Se trata de buscar un equilibrio con la vida personal. Por otro lado, el cocinero admite que tiene dificultades para adaptarse.
Adaptarse a otra forma de entender el oficio
Se considera un “purista del oficio”. Por eso le cuesta. Tiene que hacer funcionar el restaurante. Pero además tiene los compromisos de la televisión, posee varios locales y tiene que hacerlos funcionar bien. Y encima tiene la presión de su mujer, que quiere que él también esté ahí…

articles.title: Shrinking Hybrid Bonding Pitches Push Inspection Limits
articles.summary:
Existing inspection tools struggle to capture defects, especially those hidden at the bond interface.
Key Takeaways:
Hybrid bonding represents a paradigm shift in advanced packaging, replacing 35 µm off-chip microbumps with 10 µm pitch or smaller pad-to-pad interconnects on-chip. It can be used to join silicon-to-silicon, as in DRAM-DRAM bonding in future HBM devices, or even disparate materials like GaN-on-silicon.
This elegant process, which is available on wafer-to-wafer or die-to-wafer platforms, reduces signal delay to negligible levels while enabling smaller, thinner packages with unmatched memory/processor speeds and bandwidth. It also consumes significantly less power.
Hybrid bonding’s success depends on the performance of advanced bonding equipment, as well as metrology’s ability to verify critical alignment, cleanliness, planarity, and surface properties — both before and after bonding. Solving these challenges is proving essential to realizing the vision of true 3D integration at the bonded-chip level.
But as hybrid bonding pitches continue to scale down below today’s production levels of 4 to 9 µm, some inspection and metrology methods are struggling to meet the spatial resolution and sensitivity needed to catch all relevant defect types, especially ones buried at the bond interface. Particles, voids, overlay errors, roughness, CMP defects, and warpage threaten the bond quality between chips. Even a single particle can delaminate the top wafer from the one below, …

articles.title: Starlink Mini 2 adds a swappable battery
articles.summary:
SpaceX announced a new version of its all-in-one satellite internet terminal that integrates a dish, Wi-Fi router, and now a battery into a single device about the size of a laptop. According to some users on X who shared screenshots of invitations to order Starlink Mini 2, the dish is priced at $999, which includes a full year of Roam Unlimited service that SpaceX values at $2,100.
Starlink Mini 2 adds a swappable battery
The all-in-one satellite dish can now operate for over four hours without an external power source.
The Starlink Mini 2 will run for up to 4.5 hours on a full charge, SpaceX claims, but that can be expanded by hot-swapping in additional batteries that will be sold separately, or by connecting the dish to a 60W power source over USB-C.
Despite the addition of an integrated battery, the Starlink Mini 2 dish is thinner than the original Mini. SpaceX has managed to slim it down to 23.1mm thick, while the previous version of the Mini was 38.5mm. The Starlink Mini 2 is slightly heavier at around 3.5 pounds as a result of the added battery weight, but carries forward an IP67 dust- and waterproof rating so it’s still safe to use outdoors.
Preorders are now open “by invitation for select US customers,” according to the Starlink website, but “coming soon” to more customers and countries.

articles.title: Effect 4.0 Ships: Dependency-Free Rewrite with 5x Smaller Bundles and Long-Term Support
articles.summary:
Effect, the TypeScript framework for building production-grade applications with typed errors, structured concurrency and dependency injection, has released Effect 4.0. Published on 30 September 2026, it is the first stable version of a line that spent eight months in beta and six weeks in release candidate.
Effect 4.0 is a from-scratch rewrite of the fiber runtime, aimed at smaller bundles, lower memory use and higher throughput. The team's own figures put a minimal program using Effect, Stream and Schema at 7.1 kB against 35.6 kB in 3.x, a 5x reduction. The heap used by 50,000 fibers drops from 157.5 MB to 21.8 MB, an 86% cut, and concurrent task throughput moves from 0.71 million to 4.57 million tasks per second, roughly 6.4x. The numbers are medians of nine fresh-process runs on identical source, and as noted by stork.ai, have not been independently reproduced.
Alongside the rewrite, the ecosystem has been consolidated. Core modules from @effect/platform, @effect/rpc and @effect/cluster now live inside the main effect package, every @effect/* package shares a single version, and the core ships with zero runtime dependencies after the final removal of pg (replaced by a native PgProtocol client) and MessagePack.
With 4.0, the team has introduced a long-term support policy. Effect 4.x receives bug fixes until September 2029, or one year after 5.0 ships, whichever is later. Security fixes run until September 2029 or two years after 5.0, again whichever is later.

articles.title: La Switch 2 est trop chère ? Pour 179 €, E.Leclerc propose la première Switch avec Mario Kart 8 Deluxe
articles.summary:
La Switch 2 est sortie en juin 2025, mais la première Nintendo Switch est toujours dans les rayons. À l’approche de Noël, beaucoup de parents la regardent encore. Il faut dire qu’elle convient parfaitement pour un enfant qui découvrirait les jeux vidéos, et qui n’a pas besoin des dernières nouveautés. articles.title: Adieu aux dark patterns : l’Europe en a assez des pièges en ligne et veut vous garantir un humain au service client
articles.summary:
Digital Fairness Act : l’Europe veut interdire ces 10 “dark patterns” qui vous font cliquer, payer et rester abonné
"Je veux parler à un conseiller." Vous l'avez tapé, retapé, presque hurlé, et le chatbot vous a ressorti la même foire aux questions, smiley compris. Bruxelles a décidé de s'en mêler. Un projet de loi européen, qui a fuité deux jours avant sa présentation officielle, ferait de l'accès à un être humain un droit. Et il va plus loin : dix ruses que vous avez sûrement croisées en ligne seraient bannies d'un trait de plume.
Ce mercredi 11 novembre, la Commission européenne dévoile son Digital Fairness Act. Euronews et Agence Europe en ont lu le brouillon, et il a de quoi faire grincer des dents chez les géants du commerce en ligne. Au menu : le droit de joindre un humain au service client, un rappel avant chaque renouvellement automatique, et une liste noire de dix "dark patterns". Ces interfaces sont taillées pour vous faire cliquer, acheter ou rester abonné bien au-delà de votre volonté.
Service client : le droit de tomber sur un humain
Selon Euronews, ce droit figure dans le volet du texte consacré aux abonnements. Et ce volet a des airs de revanche. Les essais gratuits qui se muent en prélèvement mensuel dans votre dos ? Interdits sans votre accord explicite. Un rappel arriverait avant chaque reconduction, et chaque abonnement en ligne devrait afficher, bien en vue, un bouton "résilier le contrat ici".

articles.title: Buying an EV through your ABN? Here is what the lender actually checks - Tech Guide
articles.summary:
By Nick Lim, Founder, Switchboard Finance
A lot of business owners are now looking at an electric vehicle as their next work car. The spec sheets get all the attention: range, charging speed, the screen in the middle of the dash. The finance gets about five minutes at the end, usually at the dealer, usually under pressure.
That is backwards. The car is the easy part. Whether a lender will fund it, on what terms and against which paperwork, is where self-employed buyers get caught out. Here is how it looks from the other side of the desk.
The first thing a lender looks at is not the car. It is the business.
How long the ABN has been active matters more than most people expect. Many lenders want to see at least two years, some will go to one, and a handful will go lower with a bigger deposit or a stronger file. GST registration matters too, partly because it signals turnover and partly because it affects how the deal can be structured.
Then comes income. A salaried employee hands over two payslips and is done. A sole trader or company director is asked for tax returns, financial statements and sometimes an accountant’s letter. If the latest return is late, shows a loss because of a one-off write-off, or simply does not reflect how the business is trading now, that is where applications stall.

articles.title: The PlayStation Plus PC app is shutting down next month
articles.summary:
Sony is retiring the PlayStation Plus app for PC on December 10th. Sony says it will notify users directly about the shutdown. The app allowed PlayStation Plus Premium subscribers to stream certain games on PC, but according to Sony, not many people are using that perk:
The PlayStation Plus PC app is shutting down next month
Sony said less than 0.4 percent of PlayStation Plus Premium members were using the PC app.
With a very small number of eligible PlayStation Plus Premium members (less than 0.4%) using the PlayStation Plus app on PC, making this change allows us to focus on enhancing high-quality experiences that more of our members want to use. As a result, the PlayStation Plus cloud streaming app on PC will no longer be available.
PlayStation Plus Premium subscribers can still stream games on a console or on the PlayStation Portal. Sony’s decision to take the PC app offline follows reports earlier this year saying Sony is pulling back from PC and no longer plans to release PC ports of PlayStation exclusives.

articles.title: Float appoints former BDC Capital partner Jack Fraser as FinTech’s first CFO
articles.summary:
Toronto-based Float Financial has recruited experienced growth-stage technology operator-turned-investor Jack Fraser as the FinTech firm’s first chief financial officer (CFO).
Fraser began his career in banking before moving into tech operations. He previously held CFO and COO roles at Toronto’s itravel2000 and its parent Travelzest, and guided scaling Montréal-based luxury e-commerce platform Ssense as CFO from 2016 until 2020. Fraser spent the last seven years at the Business Development Bank of Canada (BDC) serving as a partner at BDC Capital’s Growth Venture Fund, where he backed and advised some of the country’s most valuable tech companies, from Cohere to Koho Financial, Hopper, and Super.com.
“My experience in hyper growth operations [at] technology companies lends very well to where Float is today, and going to for tomorrow.”
Jack Fraser, Float
Float helps Canadian small- and medium-sized businesses (SMBs) manage their spending through cards, software, and other products. Fraser joins the firm months after leading BDC Capital’s investment in Float’s $85-million CAD Series C round, raised in part to support the company’s push into AI. He said he officially left BDC two weeks ago to take on this CFO role, which he assumed last week. He described the position as “a very elegant fit” given his background.

articles.title: 99Food altera fotos de restaurantes com IA sem autorização e enfrenta reclamações
articles.summary:
A 99Food está revisando seus critérios de moderação de cardápios após restaurantes relatarem que fotografias reais de seus produtos foram substituídas por imagens criadas ou modificadas com inteligência artificial (IA), mesmo sem autorização dos estabelecimentos.
Segundo os comerciantes, o problema não termina quando as versões originais são recuperadas. Em alguns casos, a plataforma volta a alterar as imagens posteriormente, obrigando os restaurantes a revisar repetidamente seus cardápios.
As reclamações aparecem em publicações nas redes sociais e registros no Reclame Aqui pelo menos desde abril. Os donos dos estabelecimentos afirmam que as alterações podem deixar os alimentos diferentes dos produtos efetivamente vendidos, provocando insatisfação entre clientes e até pedidos de reembolso.
O que diz o contrato da 99Food sobre imagens feitas com IA?
O contrato da plataforma com os restaurantes prevê a possibilidade de aprimorar, editar ou substituir fotografias dos produtos, inclusive com o uso de IA. A justificativa apresentada é melhorar a qualidade técnica das imagens e garantir que elas representem fielmente os ingredientes utilizados nos alimentos.
O documento, porém, também estabelece condições para esse procedimento. A plataforma deve notificar eletronicamente o estabelecimento quando realizar substituições e identificar de maneira clara e visível ao consumidor as imagens geradas ou aprimoradas por IA.

articles.title: Polestar has a new look with its Formula 2030 concept
articles.summary:
Perhaps only a small percentage of Ars readers will care about the Polestar 2030 concept, debuted today by the electric automaker. Spun out of Volvo—once upon a time, Polestar was a racing team—the brand has leveraged the resources of parent-automaker Geely to create electric vehicles that marry a modern minimalist style with rewarding driving dynamics. But you now can’t buy any Polestars in the US, since Geely is Chinese, and banning Chinese-owned car brands enjoys remarkable bipartisan support in Congress.
The Formula 2030 is about the same length as a Polestar 2 but with a very low roofline. If anything, the two-box shape reminds me of the Saab Aero-X, one of the final concepts from the then-terminal Swedish automaker. (In many ways, Polestar has adopted Saab’s mantle.)
Polestar says the concept fits into its own segment somewhere between the next Polestar 2 and the Polestar 7—it numbers its cars chronologically (mostly), not based on size—although it’s not saying if the hatchback design will go into series production. Successfully packaging rear-seat passengers and a lithium-ion battery pack is something a concept needn’t worry about, after all. Rather, it’s a styling exercise, or more than one.

articles.title: ¿Qué pasará con las próximas películas y series del 'Universo DC' de James Gunn? Así queda el futuro de la saga tras su salida
articles.summary:
Contra todo pronóstico, la fusión de Paramount Skydance y Warner Bros. les ha costado el puesto de presidentes de DC Studios a James Gunn y Peter Safran. Ambos asumieron el trabajo hace 4 años con la firme intención de diseñar un nuevo universo cinematográfico y hacerle justicia a los personajes de la compañía. Pero ahora, con su salida del cargo, la incertidumbre es máxima.
Como parte de su proceso de reestructuración, Paramount informó a finales de la semana pasada a Gunn y Safran de que su trabajo en DC había llegado a su fin. Al menos en lo que a la dirección de la compañía se refiere. Y es que ambos seguirán vinculados (por el momento) a la compañía en el apartado creativo. Porque ya tenemos algunas pistas de lo que sucederá en el futuro del Universo DC.
Por lo pronto, se ha anunciado que Jeremy Latcham, un veterano de Marvel, será el sustituto de James Gunn y Peter Safran como nuevo CEO de DC Studios. Ni la compañía ni él mismo se han pronunciado al respecto de sus planes para los próximos años, pero sí se han dejado caer ciertos detalles muy reveladores.
Así queda el Universo DC tras la salida de James Gunn
De cara a las próximas películas y series del Universo DC hay tres certezas muy concretas. La primera es que se sabe que Superman: Man of Tomorrow, secuela de la película de 2025, sí llegará a los cines en verano de 2027. James Gunn vuelve a ser el director y guionista, y ya se encuentra en el proceso de postproducción tras completar su rodaje. Por tanto, volveremos…

articles.title: 31 ans d'agacement : Windows 11 teste une option pour faire taire les touches rémanentes
articles.summary:
Cinq appuis rapides sur la touche Maj, et une fenêtre s’invite par-dessus la partie ou le document en cours pour proposer d’activer les touches rémanentes. Le scénario se rejoue à l’identique, ou presque, depuis Windows 95. Microsoft teste désormais, dans les versions d’essai de Windows 11, la case qui permet de ne plus jamais revoir cette boîte de dialogue.
La faute à un flipper de 1995
Les touches rémanentes rendent un vrai service : elles maintiennent virtuellement Ctrl ou Maj enfoncées, comme une pédale qui resterait appuyée, le temps de presser la touche suivante. La fonction s’adresse à celles et ceux qui tapent d’un seul doigt ou à l’aide d’une tige tenue en bouche. Les touches filtres, elles, ignorent les frappes brèves ou répétées pour amortir les tremblements. Deux raccourcis les déclenchent depuis trois décennies : cinq appuis sur Maj pour les premières, la touche Maj droite maintenue huit secondes pour les secondes.
Lire aussi : Windows 11 27H2 pourrait être la mise à jour majeure que vous attendez tous
Charles Oppermann, arrivé chez Microsoft en 1994 pour piloter l’accessibilité de Windows, raconte avoir écrit ces boîtes de dialogue début 1995. Les enfants de Brad Silverberg, le patron de Windows 95, activaient la fonction à répétition en martelant la touche Maj dans Space Cadet Pinball, le flipper culte de l’époque. La fenêtre de confirmation est née là, présentée dans la documentation de l’époque comme une « précaution contre l’usage accidentel ». Son équipe av…

articles.title: PitchBook opens its platform to startups for free and debuts Origin deal sourcing service - SiliconANGLE

Private markets data provider PitchBook Data Inc. today opened its platform to startups for free at Web Summit in Lisbon.
Those that sign up have to share their financials. Some of that information will reach investors through the company’s new deal sourcing service, PitchBook Origin.
The launches come as more startups than ever are landing a first round. In the U.S., the 2021 record for first-time financings had already fallen by the end of September, PitchBook and the National Venture Capital Association found in their latest Venture Monitor report.
PitchBook credits artificial intelligence with part of that growth, since the technology has made companies easier to start. AI tools have also compressed investor diligence from weeks to days. Sourcing has not kept pace, the company argues, particularly where the signals are not public.
Free access for startups runs through a program called PitchBook for Startups. Founders who have bootstrapped or raised only from angels, grants or accelerators qualify as long as they are now seeking a first institutional round and can show at least a mockup of their product.

articles.title: Nigeria adopts hybrid cloud storage for postcode database

When Nigeria’s National Digital Addressing System (NDAPS) launched on October 1, it promised to replace informal, landmark-based navigation with precise 11-character alphanumeric codes. The system is designed to improve e-commerce deliveries, enable address verification for banking and identity services, and assign unique digital postcodes to addressable buildings nationwide.
Led by the Nigerian Postal Service (NIPOST) under the Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy, the initiative is intended to provide a reliable digital addressing infrastructure for the country.
TechCabal reported that technical checks of postcode.gov.ng’s public domain name system (DNS) records pointed to Amazon Web Services (AWS) infrastructure in the United States. The finding raised questions about whether a critical public digital asset was hosted abroad, just as Nigeria strengthens its push for data sovereignty.
“The system has distinct layers,” NIPOST spokesperson Ibrahim Musa told TechCabal in an email response. “Nigeria’s digital postcode infrastructure runs on both AWS and Galaxy Backbone—Nigeria’s official digital infrastructure and shared services provider—but they serve distinct functions.”
What AWS’s cloud services mean

articles.title: Un raté, une réussite historique, et déjà le troisième vol : Isar Aerospace et la fusée Spectrum s'emballent

C’est un indice précieux que vient de repérer European Spaceflight, site spécialisé dans le spatial européen. Avinor, le gestionnaire norvégien de la navigation aérienne, a publié le 28 octobre un avis qui ouvre une fenêtre de lancement pour un troisième vol, du 26 novembre 2026 au 17 février 2027. Signe d’un très probable lancement de fusée.
Un tel avis est émis pour prévenir les pilotes des zones à éviter pendant un tir, ce qui en fait une bonne indication qu’un lancement approche. Mais à ce stade, l’entreprise est restée muette sur son calendrier à court terme.
Isar Aerospace a franchi un cap important le 5 septembre : pour la première fois de son histoire, elle a réussi à placer des satellites en orbite depuis le sol européen. C’était sa deuxième tentative, après un raté en mars 2025. Dans un cas comme dans l’autre, c’était une fusée Spectrum qui avait été mobilisée.
Une troisième fusée déjà en assemblage final
Jusqu’ici, aucune entreprise privée européenne n’avait réussi à atteindre une orbite depuis le Vieux Continent. articles.title: Google quiere llevar la protección contra sitios peligrosos al modo incógnito de Chrome
articles.summary:
Google planea extender la función Navegación segura de Chrome al modo incógnito y al modo invitado. El cambio permitiría que el navegador muestre alertas ante páginas potencialmente peligrosas incluso cuando una persona navega sin guardar el historial en el dispositivo.
La novedad todavía está en desarrollo. Su presencia en Chromium, el proyecto de código abierto en el que se basa Chrome, apunta a que Google trabaja en incorporarla, aunque no confirma cuándo llegará a todos los usuarios ni si estará disponible en todas las plataformas.
Navegación segura ya funciona en la navegación habitual de Chrome. La herramienta busca advertir sobre amenazas como sitios de phishing (páginas que imitan servicios legítimos para engañar y obtener datos), malware, extensiones sospechosas, anuncios maliciosos y tácticas de ingeniería social. Entre estas últimas se encuentra el “clickfix”, que induce a las personas a realizar acciones que pueden comprometer su seguridad.
Cómo funciona Navegación segura
Para identificar riesgos, Chrome analiza las páginas que visita el usuario y las compara con listas de sitios maliciosos o potencialmente dañinos. La comprobación puede realizarse en tiempo real, de modo que el navegador tenga la oportunidad de mostrar una alerta antes de que la persona continúe en una página peligrosa.

Pero los auriculares con cable están volviendo a ganar presencia, y hay datos que apuntan a que el cambio va más allá de una moda pasajera.

articles.title: Hackers now exploit critical Barracuda ESG flaws to gain root access
articles.summary:
Cybersecurity company Barracuda Networks warned that attackers have begun exploiting two recently patched Email Security Gateway (ESG) vulnerabilities that let them run commands with root privileges.
Barracuda released security updates to address the two flaws (tracked as CVE-2026-116606 and CVE-2026-111560) one week ago.
The first stems from an Email Security Gateway (ESG) authentication weakness that can be exploited to modify an appliance's global configuration, while the second lets unauthenticated attackers inject OS commands that execute with root privileges.
Barracuda also said that successful attacks require access to the administrative user interface (Admin UI) of targeted devices and advised customers to restrict access to trusted internal networks and use appropriate network access controls to limit exposure.
"Successful exploitation requires an attacker to have access to the administrative interface of an affected product. If exploited in combination, these vulnerabilities could allow an attacker to bypass authorization controls and obtain root access to the device," the company explained.
On Monday evening, Barracuda updated the initial advisory to warn admins that the two flaws are being exploited in attacks targeting a limited number of customers.
"Barracuda immediately initiated a comprehensive remediation process and released security patches for affected products. We have identified exploitation activity affecting a small number of organizations," it warned.…

articles.title: Google Cloud Spend Caps Reach General Availability with API and Monthly Resets
articles.summary:
Google Cloud has made spend caps generally available on Cloud Billing Budgets, letting customers pause new usage of a service in a project once a monthly budget is reached, without deleting resources. The GA release adds an API, estimated live costs that trigger caps within minutes for AI services, and automatic monthly resets, but enforcement remains limited to Gemini API, the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, Cloud Run, and Cloud Run functions.
A spend cap is a budget with enforcement attached: according to the documentation, when estimated spend on the capped service reaches the target amount, new requests to that service in that project are blocked, in-flight requests run to completion and are charged, persistent resources keep running, and nothing is deleted. Usage covered by committed-use discounts is paused along with pay-as-you-go usage, while Provisioned Throughput for AI models is never halted. Billing administrators and project owners receive alerts at 50, 80, and 100 percent of the cap.
The company changed three things between the July public preview and the GA release:
- Caps can now be created, lifted, and deleted through the existing Cloud Billing Budgets API, which the company suggests wiring into project provisioning, so a new sandbox gets a cap on creation.
- Enforcement for AI services now runs on estimated live costs shown in Cost Reports rather than on settled billing data, which can lag by hours.

articles.title: New research can tell if your child is ready for their first smartphone - Tech Guide
articles.summary:
Christmas is usually the time of year when parents gift their child their first smartphone. The question is: Is the child ready to accept that responsibility?
New research from Digital Readiness Lab has revealed two in three parents say their child is ready for their first device.
The 2026 Australian Digital Readiness Index has established three capabilities that will indicate whether a child is ready for a device.
These capabilities include self-regulation, critical judgement and help-seeking.
Self-regulation is the ability to manage attention limits and emotions around your devices.
Critical judgement is being able to recognise advertising and judge information, knowing what to do when something doesn’t feel right.
Help-seeking is turning to a trusted adult when the user is upset or confused or feels unsafe.
The Digital Readiness Lab conducted a Christmas device study where it spoke to 1,039 Australian parents and carers of children aged 5 to 14.
It asked which devices they’re weighing up, what makes the device feel right for their child, how they judge readiness and what help they want with the handover of the device?
Of the two in three parents, 66.3 per cent who thought their child was ready for their first device when they were shown the three digital readiness capabilities the picture changed dramatically.
The study showed only 1 in 7 parents say their child consistently shows all three readiness capabilities.

articles.title: Agent Substrate: Advancing Kubernetes for Agents at Scale | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
AI agents spend most of their time idle, waiting on a human prompt, a tool result or a model response. Kubernetes wasn’t built for that. Running one Pod per session holds memory for sessions that aren’t doing anything, and deleting Pods between turns pays a multi-second cold start every time and loses the agent’s state. RL post-training hits the same wall.
Agent Substrate, now donated to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) Sandbox, is an open-source, security-hardened, zero-trust runtime for sandboxed agents, engineered to safely run millions of agents and tools with 10x higher density than standard containers. It multiplexes many sessions over a small pool of worker Pods. Idle sessions are checkpointed, memory and filesystem included, and restored onto whichever worker is free when the next request arrives. As agentic infrastructure fragments into proprietary runtimes that bypass Kubernetes, NVIDIA is contributing upstream to keep this work open.
This post covers which workloads suit Agent Substrate, what is being built upstream, and how the project works with KAI Scheduler and NVIDIA Dynamo components in the DSX AI Factory Platform.
The shape of an agent workload
Traditional web services run as a relatively small number of long-lived instances. Agents follow a different pattern: they wake up and take one step, running a shell command, editing a file, calling a test suite or calling an LLM. articles.title: Governo investe R$ 24 milhões para levar internet e celular a 190 localidades rurais
FDA warns GLP-1 drugs may pose risk of rare condition that causes vision loss
articles.summary:
The Food and Drug Administration is warning that popular obesity drugs—including Ozempic, Wegovy, Zepbound, and Mounjaro—may carry a “potential increased risk” of a rare eye condition that can lead to permanent vision loss.
In a drug safety communication Monday, the FDA said it will now require makers of GLP-1 receptor agonist drugs to add a warning about that risk on their drug labels. The specific eye condition it warns of is called non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy or NAION. The condition is caused by restricted blood flow to the optic nerve, which leads to swelling and cell death and ultimately damages the nerve, causing abrupt vision loss that can often be permanent.
It’s unknown how GLP-1 drugs may cause NAION. The condition is rare overall, occurring in somewhere between two and 10 people in 100,000 in the general population, according to the American Academy of Ophthalmology. These small numbers have made it more difficult to determine with certainty if there is a connection. Further complicating the potential link is the fact that the risk factors for developing NAION are common among patients taking GLP-1 drugs. The risk factors include diabetes, cardiovascular disease, high blood pressure, high cholesterol, metabolic syndrome, and obstructive sleep apnea.
Mixed data

articles.title: Sony cancels live-service shooter Fairgames
articles.summary:
Sony has canceled Fairgames, a heist game announced in 2023, according to Bloomberg. Fairgames had once been part of Sony’s big planned push for PlayStation live service games, but the company ended up canceling some planned live service titles, including in the God of War and The Last of Us franchises, and it shut down Concord shortly after its failed launch.
Sony cancels live-service shooter Fairgames
Fairgames is PlayStation’s latest cancellation as it steps back from many of its live service efforts.
The Fairgames cancellation won’t result in job cuts, and developer Haven Studios will now support other PlayStation studios, Bloomberg reports. The game was canceled following a recent test where “player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set,” according to part of an executive memo published by Bloomberg, which also cited “challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre.” Sony acquired Haven Studios in 2022.
Sony’s live service efforts have seen some success with Helldivers 2, which is also available on Xbox. Bungie’s Marathon, which launched this year, has had a rough start, but today the studio showed off some new features coming in a December update, including a new co-op PvE roguelite mode and a PvP deathmatch mode. Sony is also working on a live service Horizon spinoff, but recently rebooted it.

articles.title: Why an ex-Cohere leader doesn’t want you to call his new law firm “AI-native” | BetaKit

“We’re hiring great lawyers; to say that we’re an AI-native law firm feels like it connotes cheap and fast,” Rosenbluth said. “Nobody would describe a law firm that uses Microsoft Word as a Microsoft-native law firm.”

articles.title: LLM Reliability Layers Under Test: Accuracy, Yield, and the Limits of Verification
articles.summary:
Key Takeaways
- Reliability layers sorted answers by trustworthiness but corrected almost none; yield, right answers over all records, exposes what accuracy hides.
- Deterministic code can prove an answer wrong, never right: it catches nonexistent codes and spans missing from the post, but plausible answers still need a model or a person.
- Recognition beats generation: recalling SNOMED codes from memory, the model invented 13 to 18 percent that don’t exist; picking from a menu, it scored ten times higher.
- Determinism held: four of five model families reproduced their output exactly at temperature zero; the fifth agreed on 70 percent of mentions across three runs.
- Detection sets a hard ceiling: no layer recovers a mention the extractor missed, so the largest gains came from matching the corpus’s annotation conventions, not domain-adapted models.
The theory: More layers should mean more accuracy
Clinical notes, incident reports, support tickets, and forum posts are prose, and a language model can read them. What it produces is not dependable. Ours was right about one answer in three on the task below and reported full confidence on two-thirds of its answers; wherever a wrong answer costs something, that is unusable.

articles.title: Running AV Reasoning Models Within Onboard Compute and Latency Limits | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
Autonomous vehicle (AV) developers need reasoning models that can operate within the compute and latency constraints of an onboard system. Larger models provide a foundation for developing these capabilities, but moving them into a vehicle requires additional work to reduce model size, preserve useful reasoning, and validate performance on the target hardware.
NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Edge addresses this need with an adaptive reasoning vision-language-action (VLA) model designed for real-time operation on NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Thor. Built on the 2B Nemotron-based reasoning backbone of NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Edge and paired with a diffusion action expert, it leverages surround-camera observations, temporal context, and navigation inputs to generate Chain-of-Causation (CoC) reasoning and future driving trajectories. It reasons adaptively, generating reasoning only when needed, reducing unnecessary token generation and conserving inference compute during routine driving.
Alpamayo 2 Edge is post-trained with closed-loop reinforcement learning (RL) in NVIDIA AlpaGym, improving closed-loop driving performance by 48.9% on top of the best-performing checkpoint without closed-loop RL. Together, these capabilities give developers a strong, edge-ready foundation for bringing reasoning-based driving into an onboard stack.

NetWeaver is the core app platform that underpins SAP's business software and handles application integration, authentication, user management, and data processing.

Cybersecurity firm Onapsis, which found and reported three of these security issues, collectively tracks CVE-2026-76964 and CVE-2026-89126 as ICM2SHELL and the CVE-2026-89103 pre-auth remote code execution vulnerability as PROXYGATE.

articles.title: Binance quitte la France et facturera les comptes non vidés dès le 29 novembre : voici comment partir
articles.summary:
Début novembre, les clients français de Binance ont reçu un mail qui met fin à plusieurs mois d’incertitude. La plateforme y annonce que leurs comptes seront clôturés à compter du 31 décembre 2026 et leur demande de récupérer d’ici là l’ensemble de leurs cryptomonnaies.
En réalité, Binance France fonctionnait déjà au ralenti depuis le 1er juillet. Depuis cette date, toute société qui propose des services crypto dans l’Union européenne doit disposer de l’agrément MiCA, que l’entreprise n’a pas décroché à temps.
La plateforme n’acceptait donc plus de nouveaux clients, et les utilisateurs existants pouvaient seulement vendre ou retirer leurs avoirs. Désormais, ils sont appelés à ne plus laisser leurs fonds dormir sur leur compte.
Des frais qui pénalisent surtout les petits comptes
Le mail envoyé aux clients précise que ceux qui détiendront encore des cryptos sur leur compte le 29 novembre devront payer des frais mensuels.

articles.title: Iomega Zip Drive: Elite Floppy Disks Before USB Sticks
articles.summary:
These days, backing up your files or sharing them with others is a walk in the park. For most purposes, a cloud service will do. For sensitive or very large files, you can plug an external drive into a USB port. In the 1990s, however, things were more complicated.
Back then, most homes weren't connected to the internet, and the few that were paid by the minute to transfer a few kilobytes per second. Flash memory was reserved for premium digital cameras and, in tiny quantities, console memory cards.
IBM had standardized the 1.44MB format for lightweight, slow-spinning floppy disks with the PS/2 series. That was enough for documents and spreadsheets, but became a problem for larger file types, such as uncompressed graphical work. Software came on CDs (or many, many floppies), but CD recorders weren't affordable yet.
If you wanted to share large files between computers that weren't in the same room, your most convenient option might have been to unscrew your hard disk (we remember doing this on a very regular basis actually), a device built for spinning fast rather than traveling, and install it in the other computer.
Image credit: LGR
Years before USB drives and broadband internet, the Iomega Zip drive packed 100MB of storage into a 3.5 inch format that fit in your pocket. It let you carry all your files anywhere and gave the first generation of independent graphic designers the freedom to work on the move.

Les quotas d’utilisation sont une règle commune à quasiment tous les chatbots et autres outils d’intelligence artificielle. Après un certain nombre de requêtes, le quota est épuisé et il faut sortir la carte bancaire pour acheter de nouveaux crédits d’utilisation. Apple s’était tenue jusqu’ici éloignée de cette règle, jusqu’à aujourd’hui. Avec ses « intelligence usage packs », Apple propose un nouveau passage en caisse pour prolonger l’utilisation de certaines fonctions. Le principe rappelle celui d’une recharge prépayée, avec un compteur nettement moins facile à lire que celui d’un forfait téléphonique.

articles.title: Software Transparency Is Changing: Allan Friedman on SBOM, AI BOMs and What Comes Next
articles.summary:
Modern software is built on layers of dependencies, open source components, third party libraries and increasingly, artificial intelligence models and external data sources. For security teams, understanding exactly what is running inside an application has become less of a compliance exercise and more of an operational necessity.
That is the foundation behind the Software Bill of Materials, or SBOM.
In a recent episode of the SecurityWeek Podcast, host Brian “SchleiF” Schleifer sat down with cybersecurity policy expert Allan Friedman for a wide-ranging discussion about the origins of SBOM, how organizations should actually use the data, the emergence of AI BOMs, vulnerability management, VEX, and where software transparency may be heading next.
Friedman, who helped drive early government and industry work around SBOM, offered perhaps the simplest explanation for why the concept matters.
“Software isn’t written, it’s assembled,” Friedman said. “What’s it assembled out of? More software.”
In practical terms, an SBOM provides a structured representation of the components and dependencies that allow software to function. But Friedman emphasized throughout the conversation that producing an SBOM is not the end goal. The real value comes from what organizations, and their suppliers can do with the information.
SBOM Is About Response, Not Just Inventory

Teleport makes Beams generally available to bring AI agents into production
Infrastructure identity company Teleport today made Teleport Beams, its runtime for artificial intelligence agents that work on production infrastructure, generally available.
Beams goes after what Teleport sees as the main reason agents have stayed out of production so far. Most enterprises have not plugged agents into those systems at all, according to Ev Kontsevoy, Teleport’s co-founder and chief executive. He blamed gaps such as delegated identity and an audit trail that follows an agent from intent to action.
Sandboxes, the tool many teams reach for now, mostly isolate the agent in a virtual machine and handle its credentials. “When the cost of an error is high, traditional sandboxes don’t cut it,” Kontsevoy said ahead of the announcement.
Teleport calls each individual runtime a Beam, and every agent gets its own. A Beam carries a delegated identity inherited from the user or agent that launched it, while the agent inside starts with no standing privileges. Work begins with a proposed execution plan. That plan can be revised by a person or by a large language model acting as judge before a separate Beam runs it with only the approved roles. Reviewers then see new requests only for steps outside the plan.

articles.title: Pinterest and Intel Take Open-Source Profiling to Internet Scale
articles.summary:
Pinterest has partnered with Intel to extend gProfiler, an open-source continuous profiler that provides production performance visibility across an internet-scale fleet of infrastructure.
Pinterest claims it operates hundreds of thousands of instances supporting 640 million monthly active users, with services written in Java, Python, C++, Go, and Node.js. At that scale, even a small efficiency improvement can have significant infrastructure and cost implications. The challenge was that engineers were using separate tools such as perf, async-profiler, and py-spy, producing fragmented profiles that were difficult to correlate across languages and machines.
Rather than building another proprietary profiling platform, Pinterest worked with Intel to extend gProfiler and contribute those capabilities back to the open-source project. The collaboration adds dynamic profiling, hardware-level telemetry, wall-time profiling, and performance-counter flame graphs, while also hardening the system for large production fleets.
gProfiler acts as an orchestration layer over several existing profilers. It combines system-wide perf data with runtime-specific tools such as async-profiler for Java and eBPF-based profiling for Python, producing a unified flame graph across the processes running on a host.

Une antenne satellite « portable » incapable de fonctionner sans prise… Le Starlink Mini traînait ce défaut : pour capter Internet au fond d’une vallée, il fallait le relier par un câble à un allume-cigare, à une station d’énergie ou à une batterie externe achetée ailleurs.

Con la energía eólica ocurre una cosa: tiene un problema del que se habla mucho menos que de sus beneficios. Nos referimos a qué hacer con sus gigantescas estructuras cuando dejan de funcionar, especialmente esas enormes palas aparentemente inútiles. China lleva tiempo buscando una respuesta, y un grupo de científicos acaba de demostrar que la solución podría ser tan brutal como sorprendente.
El cementerio de los gigantes verdes. Qué duda cabe, los aerogeneradores son uno de los grandes símbolos de la transición energética, pero esconden una paradoja: sus enormes palas son extraordinariamente difíciles de reciclar. Fabricadas con fibras de vidrio y resinas termoestables, están diseñadas para resistir décadas de viento y esfuerzos mecánicos.
El problema llega cuando terminan su vida útil, porque esas resinas no pueden fundirse y moldearse como los plásticos convencionales. Las alternativas pasan por enterrarlas, triturarlas o someterlas a tratamientos térmicos y químicos costosos que pueden deteriorar los materiales. Con millones de toneladas de residuos previstos para las próximas décadas, el sector necesita algo más que espacio para seguir acumulándolos.

articles.title: Binance warns of iOS flaw that could leak crypto wallet secrets
articles.summary:
Binance is warning about a vulnerability in Apple’s iOS 26.7.1, 27.0.1, and 27.2 that could allow third-party apps to read private files stored by other apps, including cryptocurrency seed phrases, secret keys, and login credentials.
The crypto exchange clarifies that the issue is at the iOS level and does not impact only the Binance app.
“A vulnerability (worse_query) affecting iOS 26.7.1, 27.0.1, and 27.2 allows malicious apps to read local files from other apps, putting seed phrases, private keys, and login credentials at risk across the entire ecosystem,” Binance says.
At this time, no cryptocurrency losses have been confirmed, but Binance urges users to install the update immediately as a precaution.
The company recommends that users delete any unnecessary and untrusted apps and apply the latest versions for iOS and other apps.
Where compromise is suspected, Binance advises users to transfer funds to a new wallet created on a clean device and reset all active login sessions.
Public exploit available
“worse_query” is a publicly disclosed iOS sandbox escape technique that allows an application to cross security boundaries and access the storage of other applications.
Yesterday, a proof-of-concept exploit has been published that uses a tool called WQ Files to perform attacks relying on the technique. Specifically, WQ Files uses “worse_query” to browse, export, edit, and delete other apps’ data without requiring a jailbreak.

Nigerian off-grid energy startup Okra Solar has secured a US$7 million debt facility from British International Investment (BII) to accelerate clean energy access.
Founded in 2016, Okra provides mesh-grid technology for off-grid communities, combining solar generation, battery storage and smart controls so that neighbouring homes and businesses can share electricity cost-efficiently. The model delivers more power than typical solar home systems while needing less infrastructure than conventional mini-grids.
Okra currently has more than 13,000 households connected and over 2.3MW of installed capacity. The US$7 million financing from BII, the UK’s development finance institution and impact investor, will allow it to procure equipment for roughly 150,000 new connections, a more than tenfold increase, with the potential to bring electricity to 750,000 people in rural Nigeria for the first time.

Microsoft is now rolling out Automatic Super Resolution (Auto SR), an upscaling technology that competes with Nvidia’s DLSS, for the Xbox Ally X, Xbox Ally X20, and select Windows Copilot Plus PCs, the company announced today. Auto SR is also getting some new features alongside this official release.
Microsoft’s DLSS competitor is out for the Xbox Ally X and works in handheld mode
With the official launch of Auto SR, your Xbox Ally X can use Microsoft’s upscaling technology undocked and with games running at 1080p.
In April, Microsoft started testing Auto SR on the Xbox Ally X, but you could only use it while docked. The full release of Auto SR announced today now works while you’re playing handheld and running on battery, and it also supports games running at 1080p. Microsoft does note that playing in handheld and at 1080p might lead to performance that “may not be as optimal as other configurations,” but says you’ll see visual improvements “especially in older games.”
Previously, Auto SR was also limited to framerates of “around” 60 to 75fps, but support for a new Auto SR Performance mode will allow you to hit framerates of up to 120fps. The Performance mode, and new compatibility with Auto HDR, will be available through Windows updates.

articles.title: Adobe Patches 110 Vulnerabilities Across 9 Products
articles.summary:
Adobe’s November 2026 Patch Tuesday updates fix roughly 110 vulnerabilities across nine products.
New patches are available for Adobe Experience Manager (AEM), Audition, After Effects, Connect, Content Credentials SDK, Dimension, Media Encoder, Photoshop, and Premiere.
Critical-severity issues have been patched in Adobe Connect and AEM, including six Connect flaws with a CVSS score of 10.
The critical flaws include SSRF, path traversal, incorrect authorization, CRLF injection, XXE, code injection, SQL injection, and XSS issues. They can be exploited for privilege escalation and arbitrary code execution.
A total of 38 vulnerabilities have been resolved in AEM and Connect, including high- and medium-severity issues whose exploitation can lead to privilege escalation, file system read, memory exposure, arbitrary code execution, and bypassing security features.
High-severity bugs have been fixed in After Effects, Media Encoder, Premiere, Dimension, Audition, and Photoshop.
The Content Credentials Rust SDK (and the C2PA Tool) received patches for roughly a dozen low- and medium-severity issues.
Adobe says it’s not aware of attacks exploiting the newly patched vulnerabilities.
The Connect and AEM patches have a priority rating of 2; the rest are rated 3, which means they are unlikely to be exploited in the wild.
