articles.title: Google Finds that Technical Debt Can Derail Coding Agents Through "Agent Distraction"
articles.summary:
In a recent article, Google senior staff software engineer Sam Saccone and senior staff data scientist Madhuri Garikapati highlighted the cost of agent distraction, where AI coding agents get derailed by stale technical debt, such as old TODO comments, obsolete bug references, and outdated specs, leading them to embark on unrequested "side-quests".
Obsolete specs, long resolved bugs, and lagging documentation no longer rest in long forgotten corners of the codebase, but rather are unintentionally ingested as context indirecting and misdirecting the next wave of coders - the agents.
According to the authors, at best, agent distraction increases token consumption and execution time; at worst, it can lead agents to "incorrect logic and decisions". To investigate this impact, they focused on TODO(bug/...) comments, which, as they note, "tend to be left behind long after the underlying bug is resolved or abandoned".
By cross-referencing every TODO an agent encounters against the TODO's bug status and the user's prompt, we can automatically separate valid work from wasted detours at scale.
Using distributed traces from thousands of engineers and hundreds of millions of agent steps, Google found that approximately 13% of sessions exposed agents to inline TODO/FIXME references, leading agents to take action targeting the reference bug in 6% of those cases. In most cases, the prompt did not even mention the referenced bug. Furthermore, in 41% of these unprompted detours, the agent wor…

A critical authentication bypass vulnerability in Xen Orchestra is being actively exploited in attacks that could grant administrator privileges and allow takeover of XCP-ng virtualization hosts.
Xen Orchestra is a web-based management platform developed by French software company Vates, used to manage XCP-ng virtualization environments, including virtual machines, hosts, and pools.
The vulnerability, tracked as VSA-2026-062, affects Xen Orchestra and the Xen Orchestra Appliance (XOA) and allows remote attackers with network access to the management interface to bypass authentication using a specially crafted cookie. A CVE identifier and CVSS score have not been assigned yet.
According to a Vates security advisory, the flaw stems from how Xen Orchestra processes authentication tokens sent through REST API requests.
The flaw stems from how Xen Orchestra processes authentication cookies.
By sending a specially crafted cookie (authenticationToken=j:%7B%7D) containing an empty JSON object ({}), attackers can trick the platform into retrieving an existing authentication token and logging them in as its owner, without requiring actual credentials.
Once authenticated, attackers can retrieve "reusable login token IDs" through the /rest/v0/users/me/authentication_tokens REST API endpoint, which can be used for further access.

articles.title: Claude Code's "don't ask again" button is leaking passwords and API keys to public GitHub repos
articles.summary:
Facepalm: A feature in Claude Code meant to save developers a few clicks is exposing database passwords, API tokens and private keys in public GitHub repositories. When a developer tells Anthropic's coding agent to stop asking for permission to run a shell command, the agent saves the exact command, along with any credentials inside it, to a settings file in the project folder. Researchers at security firm Apiiro found that file in more than 100,000 public repositories, and about 1,100 of them contained secrets.
Claude Code asks for approval before it runs shell commands on a developer's machine. One of the options is "Yes, and don't ask again." Choosing it creates an allow rule in a file called .claude/settings.local.json. Sometimes the rule is a general pattern, but often it's the full command, stored word for word. If that command included a password, a token or a root login, the credential now sits in plain text in a JSON file inside the project directory.
Anthropic's documentation says Claude Code adds an entry for this file to the developer's global Git ignore configuration. That normally keeps Git from tracking it. But a global ignore list lives in the developer's own Git configuration, not in the repository. If the repository is cloned to a different machine, or if a folder that already holds the file is turned into a repository later, that protection may not be in place. Apiiro also reports that Claude Code often commits changes to the settings file on its own, witho…

But I worry that in trying to avoid the mistakes of the last funding cycle, we may be creating another problem: becoming so focused on traction that we lose the ability to recognise exceptional opportunities before they become obvious.
Over the past few years, the conversation around early-stage investing has shifted significantly. Founders who could once raise capital on the strength of their vision, market opportunity and team are now being asked to demonstrate revenue, customer growth, retention and sometimes even profitability before investors are willing to write the first cheque.
I understand why. The funding boom of 2021 and 2022 taught us expensive lessons. Capital became harder to raise, follow-on funding slowed, and companies built around unsustainable growth struggled to survive. Investors became more selective, and founders were forced to prioritise stronger business fundamentals.
That correction was necessary.

articles.title: Which Passing Chips Need More Testing?
articles.summary:
Manufacturers are using test data and predictive models to identify marginal chips and determine when additional screening is justified.
Key Takeaways:
A chip passes wafer sort, moves through assembly, and passes final test. Nothing in its results gives anyone a reason to hold it. Yet another chip with nearly identical results could fail in the field because of a weakness neither test exposed, whether that’s a thin timing margin, a slight resistance shift, or a combination of measurements that looks harmless when each is viewed alone.
The challenge for manufacturers is figuring out which of those passing chips deserve another look without retesting everything. Test engineers have always known that a passing result doesn’t guarantee lifetime reliability. What’s changed is how much they can learn about each device. Internal parametric measurements, manufacturing history, and predictive models can now reveal unusual behavior inside a population of passing parts, but spotting a suspicious device is just the beginning.

articles.title: Carbon emissions are down this year—but that probably won’t last
articles.summary:
Evaluating the annual global temperatures each year requires context. There is a fair amount of natural variability from one year to the next, so it’s important to focus on the trend over time. Famously, global warming did not end in 1998, as some claimed a couple of decades ago—we just had a run of La-Niña-dominated years after a very strong El Niño.
Annual greenhouse gas emissions are much less variable, having increased fairly steadily, but many complicating factors can still muddy the picture. Sometimes those factors conspire to throw a year off the trend. It looks like 2026 will be one of those years.
A new analysis led by Corinne Le Quéré at the University of East Anglia estimates that fossil fuel emissions have fallen about 0.4 percent from last year. This probably isn’t a peak that symbolizes heartening progress on climate change, though; the researchers think it’s a short-term dip driven by the war in Iran and its effect on oil prices.
Shifting percentages
This team works on the Global Carbon Project, which compiles stats on fossil fuel use and things like deforestation to track carbon emissions globally and by country. In this case, they looked at the stats and tried to pull out key underlying trends that show us what to expect over the next couple of years.

articles.title: Exploited Outlook Zero-Day Among 1,094 Flaws Patched by Microsoft
articles.summary:
Microsoft’s November 2026 Patch Tuesday updates fix 1,094 vulnerabilities across its products, including an Outlook bug that the company says has been exploited.
The zero-day, tracked as CVE-2026-124194, has been classified as a spoofing flaw and stems from Outlook not alerting users before a potentially dangerous action takes place.
Microsoft has assigned it a severity rating of ‘moderate’ and a CVSS score of 6.5. The company’s advisory provides no information about the observed attacks.
For an attack to work, the victim needs to be tricked into opening a malicious file, according to Microsoft.
“An unauthenticated attacker could send a specially crafted message file and convince a user to open it in an affected version of Microsoft Outlook. Opening the file could cause Outlook to connect to an attacker-controlled network location without displaying the usual external-content warning, potentially disclosing authentication information that could be used to impersonate the user,” the tech giant said.
The flaw cannot be triggered through the Preview Pane, Microsoft said. It also clarified, “This vulnerability discloses a user’s NTLMv2 hash to the attacker who could use this to authenticate as the user.”
The vulnerability was not publicly disclosed before the fix became available. Affected products include Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise, Office LTSC 2021, and Office LTSC 2024.

articles.title: France says Iran was behind supermarket refrigerator cyberattacks
articles.summary:
What just happened? France has accused Iran of being responsible for the recent cyberattacks that targeted its supermarket refrigerators. The incidents affected more than 700 stores in October, before other European countries were also hit. France says it will take action using "all available means of response."
On October 11 and 12, stores across France experienced cyberattacks that took control of their refrigeration controllers. The hackers remotely overrode the settings on freezers, fridges and chiller cabinets, in some cases raising temperatures to 50 degrees Celsius (122 degrees Fahrenheit), spoiling food and causing at least 15 fires. France put the cost of food losses alone in the tens of millions of euros.
At a press briefing following a G7 ministerial meeting in Paris, France's foreign minister Jean-Noël Barrot said, "Thanks to the remarkable efforts of government agencies, I am able to confirm that the Islamic Republic of Iran's Revolutionary Guards are responsible for this attack."
France identified the group behind the attacks as Shahid Kaveh, an offensive cyber unit affiliated with the Revolutionary Guards. It operates through several online personas, including CyberAv3ngers, a name previously linked to attacks on US water facilities.

When Friday arrives, does the team know what was promised, who owns the follow-up, and whether payment was received?

articles.title: Test Struggles To Keep Pace With AI
articles.summary:
Rapidly changing workloads, more test insertions, and fragmented data complicate chip testing.
Key Takeaways:
The rapid pace of change in AI models and approaches is creating confusion over what to test, when to test it, and what to monitor once chips are in the field.
Until recently, test targets and the timing for test insertions generally were determined by fab processes and the laws of physics, and the results of those tests were deterministic and quantifiable. But starting with the rollout of generative AI and the ensuing explosion of data centers, the gap has widened between the rollout of new algorithms and use models and the time it takes to deploy a chip in the field.
An increasing number of high-performance processors used in data centers, and many at the edge, are multi-die assemblies. The chips are more complex and take longer to design, manufacture, package, and assemble, and the workloads for which they are designed often change by the time those chips leave final test. Along the way, there are more test insertions along the way, each of which generates more data.
The tests are more complex and varied, as well. In addition to electrical tests, these chips need to be analyzed for mechanical integrity. AI workloads can stress one part of a multi-die assembly more than others, and they can change quickly as algorithms and use cases evolve. articles.title: PuppyGraph raises $10M to let AI agents query enterprise data as a graph - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
PuppyGraph raises $10M to let AI agents query enterprise data as a graph
Graph query engine startup PuppyGraph said today it has raised $10 million in new funding to build out its enterprise go-to-market operation.
The round follows the general release of version 1.0 of its software. PuppyGraph provides a query engine that lets companies treat data already sitting in their warehouses and lakehouses as a single graph, without first moving it into a separate graph database. The company says artificial intelligence agents running on it can work across 3,000 enterprise tables and get graph query results back in under a second.
Agent projects tend to hit trouble once they leave the pilot stage, according to PuppyGraph. The company’s own example asks which critical systems an attacker could reach from a compromised account, a question that means tracing how identities and permissions connect across thousands of tables in several systems.
A proof of concept might cover 30 to 50. Teams that scale past that find schema descriptions alone eating into an agent’s context window, and PuppyGraph said queries running several relationships deep can stall until they time out.

articles.summary:
The Angular team has shared details of a new version of its compiler, the Angular Preprocessor (ngp), which rewrites the analysis stage of the toolchain in Rust to clear the way for TypeScript 7 adoption. Alex Rickabaugh and Mark Techson announced the work on the Angular team blog in late September, shortly after Microsoft shipped TypeScript 7.0, whose Go-based rewrite removed the ts.Transformer API that Angular's ahead-of-time compiler depends on.
The existing compiler, ngc, wraps tsc and uses the Transformer API to turn decorators such as @Component and @Pipe into runtime instructions. The Go port offers no cross-language equivalent, and crossing the JS/Go boundary at every file would be prohibitive. The Angular team's answer is to decouple compilation from TypeScript's APIs and rebuild it on Oxc, the VoidZero Rust toolchain already powering Vite. The team pointed to the plan on X, framing it as a partial rewrite rather than a fresh start.
ngp runs in three stages. A Rust frontend using Oxc analyses files in parallel to discover Angular declarations and resolve metadata. The existing TypeScript template compiler then emits two artefacts, a runtime file containing the transformed component and a .ngtypecheck.ts file holding the Type Check Block (TCB) for template type-checking. Finally a downstream tool, whether tsgo, tsrs, esbuild or Rolldown, handles type-checking and JavaScript emission independently.

articles.summary:
Tuesday, November 10th 2026
AMD's RDNA 5 Inches Closer as GFX13 Support Lands in Linux Driver Patches
AMD has begun integrating its next-generation graphics IP into the Linux kernel, releasing a series of eight patches that add GFX13 support to the open-source AMDGPU driver. These patches, submitted to the mailing list on November 9 by AMDGPU maintainer Alex Deucher, contain over 12,600 lines of code, excluding the typically large header files. GFX13 is anticipated to be the graphics core for RDNA 5, although AMD has not officially confirmed this connection. However, since GFX12 has been linked to RDNA 4, it is assumed that GFX13 is the correct codename for RDNA 5.
The patches introduce version 13 of three IP blocks: the "graphics" GFX block itself, the MicroEngine Scheduler (MES), and the IMU. Artificial Intelligence
The agent evaluation playbook: Built-in, DeepEval, and AutoEval on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations
When you deploy an agent to production, one of the hardest questions is whether it’s actually working? The bar isn’t whether it runs. It’s whether it does what the business needs, at scale. Many teams will tell you they can’t really see this. They spot-check outputs, watch latency, and collect user feedback when they can get it. None of that tells you whether the agent finished the user’s task, stayed on topic across a long session, leaked personally identifiable information (PII), or quietly skipped half the steps it was supposed to follow.
Agent evaluation solves this problem. What makes this challenging is that a good score on one metric can hide a failure on another. A support agent can resolve every ticket and still expose personal information in its replies. In this case, the agent is failing although it has a high completion rate. To get evaluation right, measure the behaviors that matter for each agent, at the right level of detail.
This post shows how to do this on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. We use the AgentCore built-in evaluators together with the DeepEval and AutoEval evaluators directly from AgentCore Evaluations.

articles.title: Kalshi user who lost $308,000 on sports bets sues to get back $580,000

When it was over, Scott Bright had lost $308,781.62, while Kalshi had kept $89,651.76 in fees. He is now suing to recover more than $580,000, and his case raises a hard question: is software that matches buyers and sellers of event contracts a federally regulated exchange, or an online casino that Washington law has banned?
Bright filed his complaint in September in King County Superior Court. Kalshi wants the case heard in the US District Court for the Western District of Washington. It filed a motion to dismiss the following month and has also asked the court to put the case on hold.
The complaint lays out the account's activity in detail. Between June and August 2026, Bright funded his Kalshi account through his checking account, and the platform allegedly charged $5,589.05 in funding fees on those transfers. He appears to have put his winnings straight back into new positions. That would explain why the trading volume ended up about 45 times larger than what he deposited.

articles.title: Hackers exploit trusted AWS access to breach multiple cloud environments

A threat actor used compromised identity and access management (IAM) credentials for a Qubole big data platform's AWS account to access and exfiltrate data from multiple customers' AWS environments.
The campaign ran between October 14 and 26, and affected tens of companies whose AWS environments had IAM roles configured to trust an AWS account associated with Qubole.
Qubole is an enterprise cloud data processing and analytics platform that helps companies manage large datasets and run machine learning workloads. It also offers AWS integration to allow computing resource management.
Companies can grant third-party providers such as Qubole access to their AWS resources by creating cross-account IAM roles. Trust policies determine which external AWS accounts can take these roles, and permissions are set to define the resources and actions allowed.
Researchers at cloud security company Wiz explain that external providers use AWS’s STS AssumeRole API to obtain temporary credentials for accessing customers' resources in the cloud.
Wiz started to investigate the attack after data security and governance company Sentra shared information about suspicious activity observed in some of its customers' environments. The investigation also included cybersecurity company Mandiant.

articles.title: Cowbell unveils AI liability insurance for small businesses that deploy AI agents - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
Cowbell unveils AI liability insurance for small businesses that deploy AI agents
Cyber insurance provider Cowbell Cyber Inc. today unveiled Cowbell AI Liability Insurance, a standalone policy for U.S. small and midsized businesses that covers losses caused by the artificial intelligence agents they deploy.
The new policy is meant to deal with a problem that arises when businesses let agents move money or change customer records with nobody signing off first. Coverage hinges on a trigger the company calls an “AI Incident.” The definition takes in model drift and attacks that manipulate an agent, not just software acting without approval.
Cowbell describes an accounts payable agent misreading approval statuses and paying a supplier twice with no human check. Part of that money disappears when the supplier goes into liquidation.
Unrecovered funds like those can be covered, and the policy also pays to investigate what happened and take the agent offline. Inaccurate or unsafe output can be corrected or withdrawn at the insurer’s expense, with recipients notified.
Usage charges an agent racks up without authorization are covered too, such as when a loop goes unchecked. Cowbell also covers LLMjacking, where an outsider uses stolen credentials or application programming interface keys to run AI workloads and leaves the business holding the bill.
Claims brought by customers fall on the third-party side. Cowbell’s example there is a bookkeeping firm whose agent files client tax return…

articles.title: Your meditation headband may be feeding your brainwaves to an AI model

In brief: Companies that direct users' texts, emails, art, online behavior, and other work or private data to advertisers and AI training models have long been under scrutiny. However, a recent report highlights how similar practices in the brain-computer industry have largely flown under the radar. Some experts say consumer brain scanners can't collect much data, but others worry about what might happen if advertisers and AI companies can access users' brain activity.
A recent report from the journal Science outlines the relationship between the electroencephalography (EEG) industry and AI. It found that some companies selling brain-tracking devices aren't entirely forthcoming about where users' brain-signal data ends up.
InteraXon's Muse brain-sensing headband is a leading example. The $475 device tracks and charts users' brainwaves to help improve sleep and focus. But the company didn't inform users that it was using data from some headbands, supposedly anonymized, to train its AI model of the brain until after Science notified them.
Science also examined the privacy policies of dozens of other consumer-facing EEG companies and found that around one-third didn't clearly explain how they handle user brainwave data. Of those companies, 11 had policies that mentioned only how users interact with their websites, and four had no privacy policies at all.
A relatively little-known industry has been exploring EEG devices since long before the AI boom. InteraXon first unveiled what…

articles.title: PSI is trying to make a business out of AI-driven scientific discovery | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
David Turturean, a recent MIT graduate and a member of the technical staff at the startup lab Physical Superintelligence (PSI), used early access to Anthropic’s Fable 5.2 model to solve an 18-year-old problem about quantum computing.
“I’m totally accepting the idea that this might be the last paper I ever put out,” Turturean, who deferred plans to pursue a master’s at MIT’s prestigious computer science and AI lab to join PSI, told TechCrunch. “In a few months, like, why would you even put out a paper?”
The problem in question, the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture, concerns the ability of quantum computers to solve problems faster than classical ones. Scott Aaronson, one of the two researchers who posed the problem, writes that he doesn’t quite understand the proof but that he believes it’s correct because it was autoformalized in Lean, a coding language for math, and explained by a team of top researchers with whom PSI shared the solution.
The solution appears to close the door on one avenue quantum computers could follow to solve certain difficult problems at high speed, but not all of them. “It’s a negative result that allows people to know, okay, we’re no longer looking there,” Turturean said.
More broadly, it reflects the upheaval in the scientific world caused by AI problem-solving.

Because both platforms are closed, Kora argues, the integration stops at that point. Linux, by Kora’s account, is the only operating system open enough to be rebuilt around models and agents from the kernel up.
The core of that rebuild is an inference engine Kora calls Cortex. Selon la documentation de Google, la navigation privée de Chrome ne bénéficie pas toujours des mêmes vérifications Safe Browsing que la navigation classique. Elle se contente d’une liste stockée sur l’appareil.
Pourquoi la liste locale ne suffit pas face à des sites éphémères
Safe Browsing repose sur deux mécanismes. Le premier est une liste d’adresses connues comme dangereuses (hameçonnage, logiciels malveillants), stockée sur l’appareil. Le second est une vérification en temps réel. Dans ce cas, Chrome interroge Google pour savoir si l’adresse visitée figure parmi les menaces recensées à cet instant. Avec la protection standard, réglage par défaut, le navigateur consulte d’abord une liste locale de sites réputés sûrs avant de lancer cette requête, laquelle passe par un serveur de confidentialité chargé de masquer l'adresse IP de l’utilisateur.
En mode Incognito, Chrome peut se replier sur la seule liste locale des sites dangereux. Pour éviter de se faire repérer, de nombreux sites malveillants restent en ligne moins de 10 minutes. articles.title: We Source Chips Others Cannot Secure, 2026 - EE Times
articles.summary:
In 2026, the global electronic components supply chain continues to navigate choppy waters.
For buyers and engineers across Europe and the US, the real headache is never simply “can I get the part?” It is four problems hitting at once: unstable lead times, volatile pricing, counterfeit and refurbished parts flooding the market, and critical part numbers that can go out of stock without warning. When a single chip’s lead time stretches from 8 weeks to 20, a production line grinds to a halt. When a batch of parts of unknown origin slips into a BOM, the cost isn’t just money — it’s delivery credibility and customer trust.
Over the past three years, the industry has been through a full downcycle. Demand contracted, inventory piled up, and prices fell. Many buyers thought they could finally breathe easy. But the reality is the opposite: the colder the market, the more traps appear in the supply chain. Mainstream part numbers are readily available with short lead times — but the moment you hit an allocation-constrained, end-of-life, or hard-to-find part, lead times can jump from weeks to months overnight. Por si acaso, Portugal ya ha ordenado cerrar sus colegios este miércoles y muchas escuelas a este lado de la raya han seguido el mismo camino. El problema es que una ciclogénesis explosiva como la que tenemos encima es un terreno abonado para que se repita.
Y, aunque no lo haga, rachas de 140 km/h en superficie sobre la Península es algo muy poco habitual (más allá de cabos y cumbres). Y extremadamente peligroso.
Lo que está confirmado. AEMET explicaba este martes que la presión en el centro de Charles va a caer 19 hectopascales en 24 horas. A las latitudes por las que se mueve (entre 35 y 38° N) el listón de la ciclogénesis explosiva está entre 15,9 y 17,1 hPa; así que lo salta. No de forma extremadamente llamativa, pero lo hace.

articles.title: Google Fi adds support for a second 5G network, won't say which one
articles.summary:
Google has announced a “super network” upgrade for its Fi cell service. For the past few years, Google Fi has operated exclusively on the T-Mobile network, but now it’s adding support for a second 5G network. Oddly, Google refuses to say which one.
Google’s MVNO (mobile virtual network operator) launched in 2015 as Project Fi with support for both T-Mobile and Sprint service. The service initially only worked on Google’s Nexus phones, which would switch between networks based on signal strength. After T-Mobile absorbed Sprint, Fi switched to being a single-network service in the US while continuing to hop between networks for international travel.
With the super network, Google Fi is again a dual-carrier service stateside. Phones connected to Fi will be able to hop between T-Mobile 5G and a different 5G network to provide the best possible connectivity. Google’s blog post announcing the change conspicuously doesn’t mention either network, saying only that it supports “two of America’s best 5G cellular networks.”
We know one of them is T-Mobile, and the other must be either AT&T or Verizon. When reached for comment, a Google spokesperson declined to name the second network, which is odd. Looking at the Fi coverage map, my best guess for the super network partner is Verizon. The shape of unserved regions is a closer match than AT&T, but carriers do tend to fudge the fine details of these maps.

The company today announced the Hedra Model Factory, a new post-training and inference platform that enables the recursive self-improvement of AI models, or RSI for short, designed specifically to power autonomous robots and other machines.
Hedra says that physical AI requires a very different and more specialized form of intelligence that can enable robots and other real-world hardware systems to perform very specific tasks, such as packing irregular-shaped parcels onto palettes. But training all of those models is not feasible, given the vast amounts of data required to create them. That’s why Hedra wants to use RSI to adapt existing models to new tasks.
RSI is a relatively new technique in AI that describes systems that can autonomously evaluate, train and then improve their own architectures. There has been a lot of research into these systems in frontier AI labs, but until now no one has managed to apply that continuous loop to the physical world.

articles.title: What happens to mathematics when AI becomes an oracle?
articles.summary:
Our modern world runs on math, from social media algorithms, package delivery, and weather prediction to medical imaging and machine learning. The rise of computers helped fuel its dominance, enabling us to work with increasingly large numbers that would otherwise be beyond the capacity of our finite human brains. But with the rise of large language models, AI chatbots, and, soon, quantum computing, so-called “big math” is beginning to outstrip its creators entirely. What that means, and how we might adapt, is the focus of a new book, Big Math: The Hidden Codes That Run Our World, by applied mathematicians Steven Strogatz and Alex Townsend.
Strogatz is perhaps best known in his field for his co-authorship of a seminal 1998 paper with Duncan Watts on the collective dynamics of small-world networks. He has also studied chaos theory as applied to physics, the geometry of supercoiled DNA, and the biological collective oscillators, such as swarms of synchronously flashing fireflies and crickets that chirp in unison. In 2005, Strogatz extended his study of synchronicity to the crowds that caused the wobbling of London’s Millennium Bridge.
An award-winning communicator, Strogatz wrote three series of columns on mathematics for The New York Times in 2010, 2012, and 2025 and hosted a podcast for Quanta magazine from 2020–2021. He has written four popular books: Sync (2003), The Calculus of Friendship (2009), The Joy of X (2012), and the New York Times bestseller Infinite Powers (2019)…

Nitori, often called the “IKEA of Japan,” is a major furniture and home furnishings retailer that operates 879 stores in Japan and another 219 stores across China, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand, Singapore, and Hong Kong. The firm has an annual revenue of $5.8 billion.
According to the company's notification, the incident impacts individual customers, corporate members, and non-members who placed orders through official Nitori stores and online shops.

The Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) approved the construction permit application for four of X-energy’s Xe-100 reactors at a Dow chemical plant in Texas. X-energy says the approval is the first for an advanced nuclear reactor at an industrial site in the United States.
The U.S. nuclear industry has pinned its hopes on small modular reactors — or SMRs — like those being developed by X-energy. By shrinking the reactor, proponents say it will speed construction and reduce costs, though those advantages have yet to be proven. No SMR is currently in operation in the U.S., and X-energy says Dow’s reactors won’t be operational until the early 2030s.

“The NRC only accomplished this feat by pushing consideration of critical safety questions to a later date—issues the NRC should’ve fully resolved before green lighting construction,” Edwin Lyman, director of nuclear power safety for the organization, said in a statement.

Staera launches with $4.6M to develop an optical interconnect for chiplets
Staera Semiconductor Inc., a startup that develops technology for linking together chiplets, launched today with $4.6 million in pre-seed funding.
Singaporean fund Openspace Capital led the investment. It was joined by SGInnovate, Black Kite Capital, 28 Holdings, In Group and financial software company Decimus Technologies.
High-end artificial intelligence accelerators comprise multiple chiplets, silicon dies that each perform a narrow set of tasks. They’re linked together by a kind of miniature network that also functions as the host accelerator’s base layer.
That miniature network takes the form of an interposer, an advanced device that sometimes includes computing circuits, or a bridge. A bridge is essentially a small interposer that costs less to make.
Interposers and bridges both use tiny copper wires to move data between the chiplets they connect. San Francisco-based Staera hopes to replace those copper wires with optical links. According to the company, optical technology is faster and uses less power. It can also transmit data over longer distances without slowing down, which enables chipmakers to build bigger accelerators.

Grand Theft Auto VI Runs at 30 FPS, PS5 Pro Gets PSSR and Ray Tracing
Grand Theft Auto VI is now available for pre-load for gamers who pre-ordered the game, allowing them to start the download. With the game launching on November 19, Rockstar has confirmed that it will run at 30 frames per second on consoles, utilizing their integrated graphics for maximum visual fidelity. This means that while the studio has invested significant resources to maximize the performance of these console graphics cards, the game will be capped at 30 FPS to ensure stability and optimal visual quality. Current generation consoles are limited to 30 FPS, although some will receive additional features.
For instance, Sony's PlayStation 5 Pro will offer gamers PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) and ray-traced shadows, exclusive to that console. OpenAI is going for a charm offensive and promising transparency but faces stiff opposition to its plans

Following a midterm election in which opposition to data centers became a significant political issue, OpenAI promised in a new announcement to be more transparent and listen more carefully to the communities expected to host them.
Under its new community infrastructure commitments, OpenAI says it will provide more information about construction plans and their environmental effects. The company is also moving away from requiring public officials to sign non-disclosure agreements during negotiations, with limited exceptions for sensitive information. It's a notable change for an industry that has often approached local development as though the promise of technological progress should be enough to overcome almost any objection.

articles.title: Honda invests $166M to upgrade Ontario plant to make hybrids
articles.summary:
Honda Canada has announced that it will invest C$166 million into retooling and expanding its Alliston, Ont. plant, which will provide more than 4000 jobs and expand its hybrid-electric production.
As noted by CP24, the announcement is part of a broader $867 million commitment to bolster its North American manufacturing network and to meet the growing demand for hybrid vehicles.
Now, this announcement comes following Honda’s decision to indefinitely pause its $15 billion EV expansion in Alliston, and after the automaker reported a $2.7 billion full-year loss, which the company says was attributed largely to the high costs of developing electric vehicles and shifting market conditions — choosing instead to focus on hybrids.
Speaking of hybrids, when Honda announced that it was shifting away from its EV plans, the company shared that it plans to launch 15 new Honda and Acura hybrid models globally by the year 2030, with North America as a key market.
The company says that investments in manufacturing facilities across Canada, Ohio, Alabama, and Georgia will help support production of these vehicles in North America.
Specifically, the Ohio plant (built between Honda’s existing East Liberty and Marysville assembly plants) is set to open in 2029 pending final government approvals, and will be able to manufacture nearly 240,000 vehicles annually.
Honda also shared that it is working with both the federal and Ontario governments on the project.

Raoof’s firm, Proximal Ventures, is betting that AI can transform the tools, infrastructure, and services that support drug development.
Pharmaceutical companies have historically outsourced various stages of drug development to specialized service providers, from synthesizing thousands of molecular compounds and figuring out how to manufacture drugs at scale to analyzing clinical trial data.
“For a long time, the assumption was that pharma is not a great buyer of software, but a really good buyer of services,” Raoof told TechCrunch.
Raoof believes AI could automate much of that work, creating an opportunity for startups to capture billions of dollars in pharmaceutical industry spending. By using AI, these companies could deliver the same services at a lower cost and in significantly less time, he said.
Some of the most valuable applications of AI so far have been in service-oriented industries like law and finance, Raoof said. He sees similar opportunities in pharmaceutical services.

Bislang galt das äußere Sonnensystem in der Wissenschaft als ein äußerst stabiles Konstrukt, bei dem selbst nach dem Tod der Sonne in einigen Milliarden Jahren die äußeren Planeten für weitere 30 bis 100 Milliarden Jahre geordnet auf ihren Bahnen verbleiben sollten. Zwar wird unsere Sonne als Roter Riese vermutlich die inneren Planeten zerstören, doch erst externe galaktische Einflüsse galten als endgültige Bedrohung für Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus und Neptun.

Wie aus einer im Fachmagazin The Astrophysical Journal Letters veröffentlichten Studie hervorgeht, destabilisieren sich die Planetenbahnen vermutlich hundertmal schneller, als es bisherige Simulationen prognostiziert haben.
Ungleichmäßiger Masseverlust verändert die Bahnen

Die wahre Ursache für die nun berechnete beschleunigte Destabilisierung liegt jedoch in eben jener Art und Weise, wie der sterbende Stern seine Masse verliert.

articles.title: Un objet mystérieux accélère dans l’espace et les scientifiques ne savent pas pourquoi : le Japon a envoyé une sonde à ses trousses
articles.summary:
Un objet mystérieux accélère dans l’espace et les scientifiques ne savent pas pourquoi : le Japon a envoyé une sonde à ses trousses
Il mesure onze mètres, tourne sur lui-même en un peu plus de cinq minutes et dévie de sa course comme si une main invisible le poussait. Les astronomes pensaient avoir trouvé l'explication : une comète déguisée, propulsée par de la glace cachée. Une nouvelle étude vient de la mettre à mal. La sonde japonaise Hayabusa2 file vers lui pour un rendez-vous en 2031, et en attendant, une hypothèse digne d'un roman d'espionnage refait surface : un engin soviétique perdu en 1988.
L'objet s'appelle 1998 KY26. Le programme Spacewatch l'a repéré le 28 mai 1998 depuis l'Arizona. En 2023, une équipe menée par l'astronome Darryl Seligman a relevé dans sa trajectoire une accélération perpendiculaire au plan de son orbite. La gravité ne l'explique pas, et elle est trop forte pour venir de l'effet Yarkovsky, cette infime poussée que produit la chaleur réémise par un astéroïde.
Pourtant, l'objet n'a ni queue ni nuage de poussière. Les chercheurs y ont vu une "comète sombre", qui rejetterait de la vapeur d'eau sans qu'on la voie. La JAXA, l'agence spatiale japonaise, en a fait l'ultime destination de Hayabusa2, la sonde qui a rapporté sur Terre des fragments de l'astéroïde Ryugu en 2020.

articles.title: Sicherheit für dein Heimnetz: Wie lange bekommt deine Fritzbox noch Updates?
articles.summary:
Sicherheit für dein Heimnetz: Wie lange bekommt deine Fritzbox noch Updates?
Fast jedes Update bringt neue Funktionen auf Router, Repeater und andere Geräte von Fritz. Die FritzOS-Version 8.4o bringt etwa einen DNS-Filter auf Fritzboxen, mit dem sich bestimmte Werbeanzeigen, etwa auf Smart-TVs, ausblenden lassen. Die nächste Aktualisierung, FritzOS 8.50, steht auch schon für mehrere Router bereit. Doch wie lange geht das noch so? Nicht nur Smartphone-Besitzer:innen wissen, dass es irgendwann ein Ende hat mit dem Software-Support.
Bei Routern kann der besonders schwer wiegen, wenn kritische Sicherheitslücken nicht mehr geschlossen werden. Schon mehr als einmal hat ein Hersteller in diesem Fall zur Entsorgung geraten. Allerdings lässt sich schwer vorhersagen, wann ein Router oder entsprechendes Zubehör keine Updates mehr bekommt. Fritz hat deswegen für seine Kund:innen eine Liste veröffentlicht, die genau das beantwortet.
Fritz mit Software-Support bis in die 2030er
Die gute Nachricht: Wer ein halbwegs aktuelles Modell besitzt, muss sich in naher Zukunft keine Sorgen machen, plötzlich ohne Software-Updates darzustehen. Viele aktuelle Modelle unterstützt Fritz bis Anfang 2033. Elon Musk’s Terafab targets 1 million wafers a month after 2032 — planned 700,000 monthly memory wafers could rival Samsung’s entire estimated DRAM production capacity
Terafab’s procurement team reportedly has already been to Japan, asking some toolmakers to deliver within months.
Elon Musk’s Terafab, a joint venture of Tesla and SpaceX, has informally told equipment makers it is seeking to produce 1 million wafers per month after 2032, according to Financial News. About 70% of this output, or 700,000 wafers, is planned to go to memory, with more than 300,000 going to logic chips. Terafab’s procurement team has already visited Japan to ask some local toolmakers for delivery within months. The memory allotment would rival Samsung’s estimated DRAM production capacity if it were all of that type.
Samsung’s DRAM capacity was estimated last year at 650,000–700,000 wafers a month, while SK hynix is reportedly at about 550,000, with about 1 million a goal by 2030. The comparison has to be taken in context, as Terafab’s 700,000 measures all of its expected memory output, which could be NAND or DRAM, while the Samsung and SK hynix figures measure only DRAM. As it is, the memory portion alone would be 3.5 times the reported 200,000 at SK hynix’s Wuxi fab in China.

articles.title: OpenAI, Anthropic face new oversight as New York’s AI safety law takes effect | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
New York is gearing up to enforce one of the country’s most significant AI safety laws. The state opened a registration portal Tuesday, with which large frontier AI developers like Anthropic and OpenAI will be required to register by January 1, 2027.
The RAISE Act, New York’s safety and transparency bill, kicks in at the start of the year. It mandates that large frontier developers — companies with more than $500 million in annual revenue — have to publish safety frameworks on their websites, report critical safety incidents within 72 hours, and issue public model transparency reports.
The newly formed Office of Digital Innovation, Governance, Integrity, and Trust (DIGIT) will implement the RAISE Act and oversee large frontier AI labs. Penalties can be as high as $1 million for one violation and $3 million for subsequent violations.
The state also can bring enforcement actions against companies that fail to register with the new portal, though a spokesperson declined to provide specifics.
“Tech moguls tell us that their vision for AI is inevitable,” Governor Kathy Hochul said Tuesday during a press briefing. “They tell us get on board or get left behind… That any collateral damage is worth it as long as we win the race to the AI cliff.”
On Tuesday, Hochul also launched the New York Center for AI Responsibility and Research based at State University of New York’s Binghamton University. The center will independently evaluate the safety, security, and operation of advanced AI sy…

Here We Slop Again: Thanks to the enormous amount of data used to train modern large language models, fame-seeking young devs and AI enthusiasts are now hard at "work" on previously unthinkable porting projects. Even GTA VI, one of the most anticipated games in recent years, might not be immune to the brute-force power of vibe-coding chatbots.
Former Rockstar North technical director Obbe Vermeij thinks a PC port of GTA VI could arrive sooner than expected, because Rockstar and Take-Two may want to get ahead of any attempt to put an unofficial version of the game out on the platform.
Vermeij, who left the studio in 2009 and admits he doesn't know what Rockstar is thinking, said generative AI has really changed the world, and that it's now a big question for developers and publishers how to avoid having their games duplicated by chatbots.
In a recent interview with Rock Paper Shotgun, Vermeij explained that most publishers prefer to launch on all available platforms at once, since that means paying for only one marketing campaign. Grand Theft Auto has always lived by its own rules, so Rockstar sticks with consoles first. However, AI-assisted "decomps" are essentially jeopardizing any effort to keep major releases such as GTA VI locked away from the PC.

La función es útil para quienes usan WhatsApp Web en una oficina, un PC familiar, un cibercafé o durante un viaje. Hallar un aparato desconocido no prueba por sí mismo que alguien haya leído los chats, pero exige actuar de inmediato: cerrar esa conexión y revisar las medidas de seguridad de la cuenta.
Cuál es la función que permite revisar todos los accesos a la cuenta de WhatsApp
La herramienta se llama “Dispositivos vinculados”. Allí aparece el listado de computadoras, tabletas y navegadores asociados a la cuenta de WhatsApp. Cada registro permite identificar el tipo de aparato conectado y, según el caso, conocer cuándo se produjo la última actividad.
La revisión se realiza desde el teléfono donde está instalada la aplicación. En Android, hay que abrir WhatsApp, tocar el ícono de tres puntos verticales de la parte superior derecha y elegir “Dispositivos vinculados”. En iPhone, la opción suele estar dentro de la pestaña de configuración de la aplicación.

articles.title: Anthropic ha descubierto lo que mi madre ya sabía: la IA cuida mejor las cosas cuando cree que son suyas
articles.summary:
No es que tuviese demasiadas cosas cuando era pequeño, en mi familia nos apretábamos el cinturón. Por eso cuidaba cada juguete como si fuera un tesoro, porque realmente era tal que así: si rompía algo, me quedaba sin jugar. Esto es algo que siempre me recalcó mi madre: "Cuídalo, que es tuyo". Y es justo lo que Anthropic recomienda decirle a Fable 5.2.
La receta para mejorar el código. Todos los modelos de IA alucinan en mayor o menor medida, lo mejor es no fiarse por completo de cualquier cosa que creen. En el código también se aplica, incluso cuando quien está detrás son grandes modelos como el nuevo Fable 5.2. Y este tiene, además, una manía: si no sabe de quién es el código, añade al que ya existe aunque se repita. Y avisa de los problemas detectados en lugar de arreglarlos.
Según ha explicado Anthropic en su guía para sacarle partido al modelo, Fable 5.2 se comporta de forma distinta según según de quién crea que es el código que está tocando. Un detalle que destacó Simon Willison.
En palabras de la propia Anthropic:
"Cuando el prompt dice que la base de código es del propio modelo, este a menudo fusiona el código repetido y hace correcciones relacionadas sin que se lo pidan".

WhatsApp’s next chapter could transform it from a messaging platform into an everyday digital services hub, combining richer conversations, seamless payments and AI-powered assistance.

articles.title: The US military seems to be getting nervous about the launch supply crunch
articles.summary:
The US military is taking a new approach to prop up commercial launch companies as SpaceX looks to wind down its Falcon rocket program, suggesting defense officials see the workhorse rocket’s retirement as a potential national security risk.
The Pentagon’s Office of Strategic Capital has twice in the last two weeks announced it was sending cash to two of SpaceX’s competitors in the launch business. First, on October 26, the office announced a $150 million conditional loan commitment to Stoke Space. Military officials revealed a second $150 million Pentagon loan Tuesday for Rocket Lab.
Stoke Space and Rocket Lab are the first two launch companies to receive significant support from the Office of Strategic Capital (OSC), an organization established in 2022 to infuse companies developing “vital” national security technologies with capital. OSC has been on a loan spree in recent weeks, committing hundreds of millions of dollars to companies specializing in batteries, drones, and semiconductors. In the space sector, the office also provided a $150 million loan to LeoLabs, a commercial satellite tracking company, for production and deployment of radar units.
SpaceX, the Pentagon’s leading launch provider, has stopped taking commercial orders for Falcon 9 launches after 2028 as the company shifts its focus to the next-generation, super-heavy-lift Starship rocket. Former PlayStation boss Shawn Layden thinks fixing that would mean more to players than a faster PS6. "I think we have enough power in the machine," he said. "The innovation needs to come not from making PS6 for $1,200 – it's to make another PS5 for $300. Now, that would be true innovation."
Layden made the case on a recent episode of The Trophy Room podcast. He ran PlayStation's US business and later its worldwide studios before leaving Sony in 2019, so he's seen a few console generations from the inside.
The PS5, meanwhile, has gone the other way. "This is the first platform that I've seen that has gone up in price over time," Layden said. Since April, a standard model has cost $649 in the US. Even the Digital Edition now goes for $599, up from $399 at launch. That's mostly because AI data centers are soaking up the memory chips consoles rely on.

articles.title: „Wir haben es schon einmal geschafft”: Was Österreichs Protestkultur über Tech-Widerstand lehrt

„Another Zwentendorf is possible“ steht in großen schwarzen Lettern auf dem Transparent vor mir. Ich bin in Linz, der drittgrößten Stadt Österreichs, und besuche das Ars-Electronica-Festival. Rund 30 Kilometer außerhalb, in Kronstorf, entsteht das größte Rechenzentrum des Landes. Ein Hyperscaler, der einmal so viel Strom verbrauchen soll wie die Hauptstadt Wien.
Der Standort ist das Gegenteil einer Millionenmetropole. Das beschauliche Kronstorf zählt gerade einmal 3500 Seelen. Vor 18 Jahren hat der Tech-Konzern Google dort ein Stück Land erworben und mit den Jahren wurde das Vorhaben immer größer. Was einst als Cloud-Infrastruktur und wirtschaftliche Chance angepriesen wurde, steht heute vor allem für zwei Buchstaben: KI. Das Rechenzentrum soll die enormen Rechenkapazitäten dafür bereitstellen.
Die ökologischen Kosten trägt die Region. Nicht einmal eine Umweltverträglichkeitsprüfung ist vorgesehen. Und das, obwohl das Rechenzentrum erwärmtes, mit Chemikalien versetztes Wasser in die Enns leiten wird. Die Genehmigungen sind erteilt, die Bagger rollen. Seagate ressuscite le concept de disque dur hybride avec le FireCuda Forge, un disque dur externe doté d’un logement pour SSD afin d'accélérer les temps d’accès et les débits. Le fabricant entend ainsi répondre à la pénurie de puces mémoire.
Il ne vous aura pas échappé qu'avec la "RAMpocalypse" ou "RAMgeddon" (pénurie de mémoire provoquée par l'essor de l’IA), les prix de nos modules de stockage ont tout simplement explosé. Ainsi, un simple SSD de 1 To se négociait il y a un peu plus d’un an sous la barre des 100 € ; il se retrouve aujourd’hui aux alentours des 230 €. Dès lors, pour stocker une quantité importante d’informations, il faut soit casser un PEL, soit se rabattre sur une solution de stockage plus abordable, bien qu’également en hausse : les disques durs mécaniques.
Le disque dur mécanique présente toutefois des inconvénients notoires : des temps d’accès bien plus longs que ceux d’un SSD, des débits plus faibles limités au SATA à 6 Gb/s (600 Mo/s théoriques) et des pièces mobiles (plateaux, têtes de lecture) qui émettent du bruit. Bref, si la démocratisation des SSD avait relégué le HDD au stockage d'archivage, celui-ci est en passe de faire son retour pour des questions d’économie.

articles.title: AMD launches Zen 6 Epyc 9006 series with up to 256 cores, 512 threads, and TSMC N2
articles.summary:
Highly anticipated: AMD has fully pulled back the curtain on its first Zen 6 CPU lineup. Debuting with Epyc server chips, the new architecture offers up to 256 cores and 512 threads at the top end, and AMD has promised substantial upgrades in AI, GPU hosting, and per-watt performance.
AMD's first Zen 6 Epyc processors, labeled the 9006 series and codenamed Venice, are now shipping to server clients, with SP7 systems arriving first and SP8 following in the first half of 2027. The company recently published the full technical specs for every SP7 and SP8 CPU in the lineup, mainly promoting their usefulness for AI workloads.
As expected, AMD's new flagship Epyc 9996 raises the maximum core count to 256, with 512 threads, clocked at up to 4.1GHz. With 1GB of L3 cache, it sits at a 2.55GHz base clock and defaults to 600W, though it can be configured down to 400W.
AMD's rack-density comparisons also reference a 400W, 256-core 9956, but that chip isn't on the published list. According to AMD's internal benchmarks, the 9996 at least doubles the Intel Xeon 6980P's performance in some tasks and more than triples it in others.
Early independent testing backs up the scale of the gains: Tom's Hardware measured a dual 9996 server at up to 93% faster than a dual Epyc 9965 in SPEC CPU 2026's intrate test. Non-deterministic agents break the rules traditional software security was built on
AI agent security has become the critical gating factor for enterprises that want autonomous software doing real work.
Unlike chatbots that answer questions, agents take actions, and every tool or credential they touch widens the potential damage. To that end, Red Hat Inc. has spent the past year building guardrails for that shift, including a sandbox for OpenClaw agents. The complexity lies in the fact that agents break the assumptions traditional software security was built on, according to Joe Fernandes (pictured, right), vice president and general manager of Red Hat AI at Red Hat.
“For forever, we’ve been building software, but that software is deterministic. It does what we program it to do,” Fernandes said. “Agents are different. They’re non-deterministic; you’re giving them a goal. You don’t know what actions they’re going to take to get to that goal.”
Fernandes and Jessica Forrester (left), senior distinguished engineer and chief architect of Red Hat AI at Red Hat, spoke with theCUBE’s John Furrier and Rebecca Knight at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon NA, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. articles.title: Bluetooth® High Data Throughput: The Future of Wireless - EE Times
articles.summary:
The world is generating, sharing, and processing more data than ever before. Applications are becoming more sophisticated, and user expectations continue to rise.
More of the experiences people, businesses, and industries rely on every day are wireless. From premium audio experiences to immersive computing, industrial systems, advanced peripherals, and emerging AI-driven applications, wireless connectivity is increasingly required to support more devices, more data, and higher expectations with every new generation of products.
Keeping pace with these demands requires more than speed alone. It requires the capacity to communicate larger volumes of information with greater efficiency and reliability. Bluetooth® High Data Throughput (HDT) was designed to meet this opportunity.
What is Bluetooth® High Data Throughput?
Bluetooth HDT introduces a new physical layer (PHY) that significantly increases the amount of information devices can exchange while continuing to operate within the same channel bandwidth and spacing used by existing Bluetooth LE PHYs. Higher throughput is achieved primarily through greater spectral efficiency, using higher-order coherent modulation and forward error correction to support multiple data rates up to 7.5 Mbps.
By increasing the maximum supported bit rate to 7.5 Mbps, nearly four times that of the Bluetooth LE 2M PHY, HDT expands the Bluetooth performance envelope across speed, capacity, energy efficiency, and reliability.

articles.summary:
AMD Zen 6 EPYC ‘Venice’ deep dive and benchmarking – 9686F outclasses Nvidia’s Vera, dual EPYC 9996 with 1,024 threads delivers up to 93% performance gain gen-on-gen
Our first look at Zen 6, both under the hood and in real-world applications.
AMD’s EPYC ‘Venice’ CPUs are the first to debut the new Zen 6 architecture, and we’ve been testing two chips from the range over the past several weeks to see how they compare to Nvidia’s Vera, and more broadly, how the Zen 6 architecture departs from Zen 5 ahead of the expected consumer-focused Olympic Ridge launch next year. Zen 5 was a ground-up redesign of AMD’s storied Zen core, and Zen 6 takes that foundation and expands it in just about every regard.
Zen 6 uses TSMC’s N2P node, but it also comes with significant architectural changes under the hood. Within the core, a redesigned vector engine pushes AMD’s SIMD performance even higher, and it now natively supports half-precision FP16 instructions alongside full, 32-bit precision. It also splits integer schedulers within the execution engine, allowing for more instructions in flight through the core.
Across the die, AMD made other significant changes. The single IOD of previous generations is now split across two IODs, giving the SP7 platform access to 16 memory channels (though at the cost of PCIe 6.0 lanes compared to the previous generation and SP8 platform).
The CCDs have been upgraded, too, for the first time since Zen 3. A standard Zen 6 CCD can now scale up to 12 cores, while…

Lo que es irremediable es el resultado: atasco, atasco y atasco día sí y día también.

Microsoft, the tech giant that is building 35 data centers around the U.S. and has plans for 134 more, has reportedly met with the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy and the National Security Council as the FCC is considering an import ban on Chinese optical transceivers. Optical transceivers are tiny modules plugged into hardware that convert their electrical signals into light signals, allowing data to be transmitted as light pulses across fiber optics. Con él se da el espaldarazo definitivo para arrancar la radio digital terrestre en España, un proyecto que llevaba décadas en el cajón y no termina de desplegarse.

Qué cambia con el decreto. El Real Decreto 958/2026, publicado en el BOE no parte de cero ya que recoge parte del plan técnico ya previsto en 1999 y seguirá vigente aplicando ciertas modificaciones necesarias para impulsar la implantación de este nuevo estándar para la radio digital en España.
Uno de los objetivos de la nueva normativa es hacer que DAB+ gane en cobertura de servicio. Esta tecnología permite agrupar varias emisoras en un mismo bloque de frecuencias de emisión, por lo que no es necesaria una frecuencia específica para cada emisora de FM. Con la publicación del nuevo decreto se amplía el área de cobertura de esas emisiones para que la señal de radio digital llegue a más poblaciones de las que la reciben en la actualidad.

Microsoft Developer Builds a GPU Task Manager to Show Which Apps Are Eating Your VRAM
Anyone wondering what is filling up their GPU's VRAM can now try gputaskman, a free, open-source tool from Microsoft VP Scott Hanselman. It runs in a terminal window with an htop-style layout and lists every process using the GPU with its memory footprint, engine activity, and loaded runtime, such as CUDA or Vulkan. A panel up top tracks utilization, clocks, temperature, and power. Hanselman shared the project on X last week and asked for pull requests.
Task Manager has shown GPU usage since 2017, and it will happily tell you that 15 GB of video memory is in use. It just won't say what is using it. gputaskman goes after that gap with a heavy focus on local AI. Its model inspector can identify the LLM a process has loaded and report its quantization, weights, and estimated KV cache cost, while Ollama and LM Studio users also get context size and proper model names. Hanselman calls it early, experimental software, and the AI breakdowns are estimates for now.On Windows, only NVIDIA and AMD GPUs are supported currently, and Intel support is limited to native Linux as of v0.3.5. There's also a native Windows ARM64 build, though it's unclear whether anyone has tested it on RTX Spark machines like the Surface Laptop Ultra. En CHAPEA 1 entraron el 25 de junio de 2023 y salieron el 6 de julio de 2024, mientras que el segundo equipo entró el 19 de octubre de 2025 y salió hace unos días, el 31 de octubre de 2026. En ambos casos se simuló una tripulación como la que viajaría a Marte, con un comandante, un ingeniero de vuelo, un oficial médico y un oficial científico. Realizaron tareas de mantenimiento de equipos, cultivo de alimentos y caminatas espaciales. Dreeze launches with $33M to recover entire cloud applications, not just their data
Israeli cloud application recovery startup Dreeze Inc. formally launched today with $33 million in new funding to bring what it calls Application Revival to enterprises running workloads in the public cloud.
Dreeze provides software aimed at what happens after a backup has done its job. Cloud-native applications depend on infrastructure, identities and secrets as well as data, and all of it has to come back in the right order before an application will run.
The company calls the manual work that follows a “recovery scramble.” Searching for credentials and rebuilding connections by hand can keep an application down for days or weeks after its data is restored.
Preparation starts well before an outage, when Dreeze’s software traces each cloud resource and dependency back to the application that relies on it. Its recovery plan comes from what is actually running, and changes to the environment update it automatically.
Configuration files, keys and application data go into an immutable, air-gapped vault, which customers can replicate across regions. When an outage hits, Dreeze rebuilds those pieces, plus the infrastructure and identities around them, in dependency order. Teams can also rehearse the full plan ahead of time as an automated test that ends with a working copy of the application, and production is left alone while it runs.

articles.title: Who Pays for AI Data Center Power Costs? How the U.S. and China Compare - EE Times

In 40 of 41 local ballot contests across 10 U.S. states on Nov. 3, voters favored limiting data center development.
The measures included bans, moratoriums, rejected zoning proposals, and nonbinding votes. Their legal consequences vary, but they signal growing scrutiny of the electricity, land, and public resources required by large computing facilities.
Meanwhile, developers are competing to secure power capacity years before their facilities will operate.
The U.S. relies on utilities, regulators, and local governments to negotiate these commitments. China coordinates computing infrastructure and energy resources through national development programs.
Both face the same uncertainty: How much infrastructure should be built before future computing demand is known, and who pays when forecasts prove wrong?
Computing moves faster than the grid
The International Energy Agency projects global data center electricity consumption rising from approximately 485 terawatt-hours in 2025 to 950 TWh by 2030. Consumption at AI-focused facilities is expected to triple.
AI accelerator generations change within years. Substations, transformers, and transmission connections are designed to operate for decades. Utilities must therefore finance long-lived infrastructure against demand forecasts shaped by a much faster technology cycle.

Advanced Micro Devices Inc. today debuted a new line of central processing units for servers.
The Epyc 6 series, which is also known as Venice, comprises 10 CPUs that are organized into two groups. The first set includes chips with a large number of relatively slow cores. The remaining CPUs feature fewer, higher-frequency cores.
Both chip collections feature optimizations designed to speed up artificial intelligence agents. AI agents run their neural networks on graphics cards and use CPUs to power their tools, the applications with which they carry out work.
CPUs also perform certain other tasks in machine learning clusters. According to AMD, Epyc 6 chips can support up to 3.3 more agents per watt than Nvidia Corp.’s Vera CPU. Additionally, the company says that its processor series significantly outperforms comparable Intel Corp. silicon.
Deploying an AI agent’s tools on CPUs with a relatively small core count can reduce software expenses in some cases. Certain enterprise applications, notably databases, are billed according to the number of cores on which they run. As a result, deploying a database on one high-frequency core is cheaper than using two slower ones that together provide the same amount of processing power.

What we learned about the hyperscalers from earnings season
Recently Amazon.com Inc., Google owner Alphabet Inc. and Microsoft Corp. reported earnings within roughly 24 hours of each other, and this earnings season told us more about long-term artificial intelligence strategy than any keynote or press release this year. Beneath the headlines lie three very different strategies.
Here’s what I took away: Amazon will be the long-term winner because its open, platform-first approach gives customers the broadest choice of models and silicon, and it’s showing that size doesn’t limit scale. Microsoft is a solid second, protected less by strategy than by the customers it already has locked in. And Google will be a distant third, with impressive technology built on a fragile business foundation and a closed, Gemini-first strategy that runs counter to where enterprises are heading.
Lesson one: AWS proved scale isn’t a speed limit
The most remarkable part of the earnings season was that Amazon’s Amazon Web Services business has found a way to buck the law of large numbers. It’s growing 39.3% at its size. AWS revenue reached $46 billion, marking its sixth straight quarter of acceleration and its fastest growth in nearly five years, putting the business at an $184 billion annualized run rate, according to Amazon’s third-quarter release.

The vulnerabilities are listed below -
- CVE-2026-123218 (CVSS score: 9.8) - An incorrect authorization vulnerability in IBM Aspera Faspex that could allow an authenticated user to craft a specific message to bypass authorization, causing privilege escalations. (Fixed in November 2026)
- CVE-2026-116779 (CVSS score: 9.8) - A code injection vulnerability in SignalWire FreeSwitch that could result in configuration and credential disclosure, arbitrary call control, and command execution. (Fixed in October 2026)
- CVE-2026-123158 aka SSHole (CVSS score: 8.1) - An unexpected status code or return value vulnerability in OpenBSD OpenSSH on Linux that could allow for authentication bypass. (Fixed in November 2026)
- CVE-2026-102895 (CVSS score: 9.8) - An improper authentication vulnerability in GPUStack that could allow improper authentication vulnerability which could allow unauthenticated administrative access, including user and model changes, persistent administrator API-key creation, disclosure of worker and cloud-provider secrets, and code execution through POST /v2/inference-backends/from-yaml. (Fixed in July 2026)

New 'BluePhishing' scam sees criminals spoof AI agents to get access to corporate environments
Be careful which agents you approve
- Researchers showed Microsoft Entra Agent ID blueprints can be abused to socially engineer malicious AI agents into organizations
- A single approved blueprint can spawn hundreds of agent identities with access to corporate resources
- Defenders should restrict third-party agent consent, apply least-privilege controls, and monitor agent creation events
When Microsoft first introduced Entra Agent ID as a way organizations can identify and monitor AI agents, it most certainly did not think it would be used to smuggle malicious agents into corporate environments. Yet, that’s where we are today.
Entra Agent ID is an extension of Microsoft Entra. It’s a system that allows companies to create AI agents, give them digital identities, and then decide which services and what data they can access. Expecting organizations to deploy dozens (if not hundreds) of these agents, Microsoft also introduced “agent blueprints”, essentially templates companies can use to create multiple AI agent identities, each with their own permissions.
In a new report, security researchers Proofpoint laid out how a threat actor could create a malicious blueprint in their own Microsoft environment and then - using classic social engineering techniques - convince a victim to approve it in their own environment. articles.title: Industrial automation startup Path Robotics raises $300M in funding - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
Industrial automation startup Path Robotics raises $300M in funding
Path Robotics Inc., a startup working to automate industrial welding workflows, today announced that it has raised $300 million in funding.
Georgian led the Series E round. It was joined by a consortium that included the venture capital arms of Yamaha Motor Co. and Navier Corp., one of South Korea’s largest tech firms. The investment gives Path Robotics a post-money valuation of $2.45 billion.
Welding tasks were historically difficult to automate because of a phenomenon called heat-induced metal distortion. It occurs when the heat produced by a welding torch warps the metal parts being joined together. Furthermore, the parts change shape again when they cool down. Those distortions are often unpredictable, which means they can throw off a robot arm that follows a static, pre-programmed welding plan.
There are also other sources of complexity. Mass produced metal parts that are based on the same blueprint often differ slightly because of manufacturing inconsistencies. In many cases, those variations make it necessary to adjust the way welding is performed. That isn’t always possible with traditional automation software.
Path Robotics has developed an AI model that addresses those challenges. Obsidian, as it’s called, is specifically designed to power industrial robots equipped with welding torches. The company says that the model can observe how metal parts change shape during the welding process and adjust it…

Canada’s geography makes covering its semiconductor industry something of a map-reading exercise. Expertise is spread across regional hubs, and the distance between complementary facilities makes collaboration a deliberate undertaking rather than something that happens over a casual lunch or networking event.
As Tyler Morhart, associate scientist and beamline lead at the Canadian Light Source’s (CLS’s) Synchrotron Laboratory for Micro and Nano Devices (SyLMAND), reminded EE Times in a recent conversation, this is an enormous country, with research infrastructure to match.
That makes Saskatchewan worth a closer look. The landlocked Prairie province has fewer than 1.3 million residents; its two largest cities are Saskatoon and the capital, Regina. The latter was recently selected for what could be one of Canada’s largest planned data center developments, to be built by Bell Canada, one of the country’s major telecommunications companies.
But the province has more to offer the rest of Canada than a convenient location for powerful AI servers: Saskatchewan is assembling a combination of computing infrastructure, quantum research, semiconductor design talent, and materials expertise that can strengthen both its own technology economy and the national semiconductor ecosystem.
The question isn’t whether Saskatchewan can do everything; it’s how well it can connect and scale up its existing strengths.

articles.title: Google Issues Chrome Security Update for Eighth Actively Exploited Zero-Day of 2026
articles.summary:
Google on Monday released updates to patch nine security vulnerabilities, including one that has come under active exploitation in the wild.
The high-severity vulnerability, assigned the CVE identifier CVE-2026-125350 (CVSS score: 8.8), has been described as a use-after-free bug in the XML component.
"Use-after-free in XML in Google Chrome prior to 157.0.8103.50 allowed a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code inside the sandbox via a crafted HTML page," reads the description of the flaw on CVE.org.
Use-after-free bugs typically occur when a program attempts to access a memory location after it has already been freed. Successful exploitation of these vulnerabilities could allow an attacker to achieve data corruption, program crashes, or arbitrary code execution.
An anonymous security researcher has been credited with discovering and reporting the flaw on November 6, 2026.
Google acknowledged it is "aware that an exploit for CVE-2026-125350 exists in the wild," but has not revealed any additional specific information related to how it's being abused in real-world attacks or who is behind them.
"Access to bug details and links may be kept restricted until a majority of users are updated with a fix," the tech giant added. "We will also retain restrictions if the bug exists in a third-party library that other projects similarly depend on, but haven't yet fixed."

articles.title: Sony canceló Fairgames, el videojuego de atracos para PlayStation 5 anunciado en 2023, tras una prueba con jugadores
articles.summary:
Sony canceló Fairgames, un videojuego de atracos en línea para PlayStation 5 que se había anunciado en 2023, informó Bloomberg. La decisión llegó después de una prueba reciente con jugadores cuyos resultados no alcanzaron los objetivos de la compañía. El estudio Haven no tendrá despidos.
Los ejecutivos de PlayStation Sean Decker y John Doyle explicaron la decisión en un memorando interno que Bloomberg publicó en parte. La prueba mostró “excelencia operativa” y buen compromiso de la comunidad, escribieron, pero los comentarios de los jugadores y la retención fueron “dispares” y quedaron por debajo de las metas.
A eso sumaron las “difíciles condiciones del mercado” en los juegos de disparos en los que los usuarios compiten entre sí. “Hemos tomado la difícil decisión de cesar el desarrollo”, dijeron los dos directivos, según el memorando citado por GameSpot y Polygon.
Un portavoz de PlayStation dijo a Bloomberg que la cancelación no implicará recortes de personal. Haven Studios, con sede en Montreal, dejará de trabajar en Fairgames y apoyará a otros estudios de la empresa, según el mismo informe.
Un juego que cambió varias veces de rumbo
Haven fue fundado en 2021 por Jade Raymond, productora de la saga Assassin’s Creed y exjefa de los juegos de Google Stadia. Sony compró el estudio en 2022. Fairgames habría sido su primer título, según Polygon.

articles.title: Alta funcionaria de la Reserva Federal de EE. UU. advirtió que las acciones podrían caer si la inversión en IA decepciona
articles.summary:
La vicepresidenta de Supervisión de la Reserva Federal (el banco central de Estados Unidos), Michelle Bowman, advirtió que las acciones podrían sufrir “una gran corrección” si la inversión en inteligencia artificial rinde menos de lo esperado. Lo dijo en un discurso el 10 de noviembre, horas después de una inflación mayor a la prevista.
Bowman dijo que los ingresos de la IA crecen rápido, pero todavía no alcanzan para pagar el mantenimiento de los modelos existentes ni el desarrollo de nuevos modelos y centros de datos. Por eso, afirmó, las grandes tecnológicas recurren cada vez más a los mercados de crédito y de acciones para financiarse.
Según la funcionaria, la deuda vinculada a la IA va camino de superar los USD 800.000 millones este año, con aumentos en bonos de empresas, crédito privado y financiamiento de proyectos. Los contratos de alquiler y otros compromisos a largo plazo podrían implicar pagos potenciales de más de tres veces esa cifra.
Bowman describió cómo se reparte el riesgo. Las empresas grandes, con buena calificación crediticia, asumieron obligaciones fuera de sus balances para que firmas más pequeñas y riesgosas las usen como garantía al financiar centros de datos y equipos. Los fabricantes de chips y las nubes, agregó, compran participaciones en sus propios clientes, algo que crea “la apariencia de financiamiento circular”.

NVIDIA May Cut TSMC Chip Orders Amid Mounting Pressure, Report Claims
NVIDIA may be slowing down its chip orders at TSMC, according to a new report from Taiwan's Commercial Times. The outlet cites unnamed supply chain sources but doesn't name a product, node, size, or timeline. Neither NVIDIA nor TSMC have commented so far, and the claims are single-sourced for now. The report frames this as NVIDIA being squeezed from inside and out. On the inside, there's Jensen Huang's November 8 email to staff, in which he apologized for an extramarital affair, and the board's independent investigation into reports that he was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. The board has said it has no reason to believe national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised. 
The outside pressure mostly comes down to export controls. The report points to tighter export reviews and H200 chips reportedly stockpiled in Hong Kong, both of which it says raise the risk of NVIDIA scaling back orders. It also cites foreign media reports suggesting that some firms approved to handle H200 could be shell companies, which feeds concerns that chips might reach China through fronts like these or middlemen in other countries.
